# Chart style -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# All charts have a transparent background, so they take on the colour of the
# page around them. In dark mode (the browser's prefers-color-scheme, sent by
# app.R as input$dark_mode) text and lines switch to light colours.
# Charts are drawn with renderPlot(..., bg = "transparent").

chart_colours <- function(dark = FALSE) {
  if (isTRUE(dark)) {
    list(
      text = "#e6e6e6",
      line = "#cfd8dc",
      grid = "#4a5560",
      accent = "#ff6b6b",
      real = "#f5f5f5",
      muted = "#a8b3bd",
      shade = "#3a4552"
    )
  } else {
    list(
      text = "#2b2b2b",
      line = "#2c3e50",
      grid = "#e3e3e3",
      accent = "#c0392b",
      real = "#000000",
      muted = "#666666",
      shade = "#d9d9d9"
    )
  }
}

chart_theme <- function(dark = FALSE, base_size = 10) {
  col <- chart_colours(dark)
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      legend.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      legend.key = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = col$text),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = col$text),
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = col$text),
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(colour = col$grid),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
    )
}

# Game engine ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# One game = new_game() then play_turn() once per turn.
# The Shiny app and the strategy bots (sim/) both use these functions, so
# whatever is tuned with the bots is exactly what students play.
#
# What a player is allowed to see is built by player_view(). Bots only ever
# get that view, never the hidden truth.

# Calendar ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Day 0 is the day the first patient is reported; each turn is one report,
# report_days apart (teaching_params.R), whatever the disease.
report_days <- function(config) {
  config$tp$report_days %||% 7L
}

turn_day <- function(turn, config) {
  1L + as.integer(turn) * report_days(config)
}

# Days of the disease's timescale to whole reports (at least `min_turns`)
days_to_turns <- function(days, config, min_turns = 0L) {
  max(as.integer(min_turns), as.integer(round(days / report_days(config))))
}

turn_date <- function(turn, config) {
  as.Date(config$tp$start_date) + turn_day(turn, config)
}

# Length of the response in days, and the day it ends
response_days <- function(config) {
  config$tp$game_turns * report_days(config)
}

response_end_date <- function(config) {
  as.Date(config$tp$start_date) + response_days(config)
}

format_date <- function(date) {
  trimws(format(as.Date(date), "%e %B %Y"))
}

# Round to a number people can judge at a glance: nearest 10,000 from 10,000
# up, nearest 1,000 from 1,000, nearest 100 below that (77,460 -> 80,000;
# 857,851 -> 860,000; 4,320 -> 4,000). Never rounds a positive amount to 0.
nice_round <- function(x) {
  step <- ifelse(abs(x) >= 1e4, 1e4, ifelse(abs(x) >= 1e3, 1e3, 100))
  out <- round(x / step) * step
  ifelse(x > 0 & out == 0, step, out)
}

# Scale London's money and capacity to another place ---------------------------
#
# Prices per test stay the same; the budget, per-report limit, measure costs,
# lab capacity, beds, tracers and isolation support grow with population,
# each rounded to a nice number.
scale_to_place <- function(tp, pop_total) {
  ratio <- pop_total / tp$reference_pop
  if (!is.finite(ratio) || abs(ratio - 1) < 1e-9) {
    return(tp)
  }
  # money: nice round numbers people can judge; capacities (beds, tests,
  # tracers): two significant figures, so they stay close to the true scaling
  money <- function(x) nice_round(x * ratio)
  amount <- function(x) signif(x * ratio, 2)

  tp$budget_total <- money(tp$budget_total)
  tp$tests$budget <- money(tp$tests$budget)
  tp$interventions$cost <- money(tp$interventions$cost)
  tp$tracing$cost <- money(tp$tracing$cost)
  tp$build_testing$cost <- money(tp$build_testing$cost)
  tp$rapid_tests$cost <- money(tp$rapid_tests$cost)

  tp$tracing$capacity <- amount(tp$tracing$capacity)
  if (!is.null(tp$sentinel)) tp$sentinel$tests <- amount(tp$sentinel$tests)
  tp$rapid_tests$kits <- amount(tp$rapid_tests$kits)
  tp$test_levels$capacity <- amount(tp$test_levels$capacity)
  tp$hospital$beds <- amount(tp$hospital$beds)
  tp$isolation$half_strength_load <- amount(tp$isolation$half_strength_load)
  tp
}

# Build the settings for one game ---------------------------------------------

game_config <- function(
    inputs,
    epi,
    mort = list(death_ifr = 0, death_delay = 0L),
    kernel_key = "default",
    susceptible_frac = 1,
    test_level = 3L,
    bio = list(asymptomatic = 0, presymptomatic = 0, delay_decay = 0.5, hosp_frac = 0.02),
    tp = teaching_params()) {

  # money and capacity scale with the place's population (1 for London)
  tp <- scale_to_place(tp, sum(inputs$pop_tbl$pop))

  # small lookup tables used every turn: plain data frames are much quicker
  tp$test_levels <- as.data.frame(tp$test_levels)
  tp$interventions <- as.data.frame(tp$interventions)

  # imports are per area each turn: keep the place-wide rate like London's
  n_units <- nrow(inputs$pop_tbl)
  epi$imports_prob <- min(1, epi$imports_prob * tp$reference_units / n_units)

  # choose the spatial kernel
  K <- inputs$K
  if (identical(kernel_key, "measles") && !is.null(inputs$K_measles)) {
    K <- inputs$K_measles
  }

  # generations of infection per report: a fast disease goes through several
  # generations between weekly reports, a slow one less than one
  gens_per_turn <- (tp$report_days %||% 7L) / (bio$gen_days %||% (tp$report_days %||% 7L))

  list(
    K = K,
    gens_per_turn = gens_per_turn,
    A = inputs$A,
    pop_tbl = inputs$pop_tbl,
    # share of people susceptible at the start (vaccination, past infection)
    susceptible_frac = min(1, max(0, susceptible_frac)),
    epi = epi,
    mort = mort,
    tp = tp,
    interventions = tp$interventions,
    test_level = test_level,
    bio = bio
  )
}

# Settings for one of the scenario presets in scenarios.R
scenario_config <- function(scenario_id, inputs, tp = teaching_params()) {
  sc <- scenario_lookup(scenario_id)

  epi <- list(
    Rt = sc$Rt[[1]],
    k = sc$k[[1]],
    imports_prob = sc$imports_prob[[1]],
    lambda_import = sc$lambda_import[[1]],
    seed_borough = sc$seed_borough[[1]],
    seed_cases = sc$seed_cases[[1]]
  )

  # delays are given in days; the game counts them in reports
  report_every <- tp$report_days %||% 7L
  mort <- list(
    death_ifr = ifelse(is.na(sc$death_ifr[[1]]), 0.002, sc$death_ifr[[1]]),
    death_delay = as.integer(round(sc$death_delay_days[[1]] / report_every))
  )

  game_config(
    inputs = inputs,
    epi = epi,
    mort = mort,
    kernel_key = sc$kernel_key[[1]],
    susceptible_frac = sc$susceptible_frac[[1]],
    test_level = sc$test_level[[1]],
    bio = list(
      asymptomatic = sc$asymptomatic[[1]],
      presymptomatic = sc$presymptomatic[[1]],
      delay_decay = sc$delay_decay[[1]],
      hosp_frac = sc$hosp_frac[[1]],
      gen_days = sc$gen_days[[1]],
      hosp_delay = max(1L, as.integer(round(sc$hosp_delay_days[[1]] / report_every)))
    ),
    tp = tp
  )
}

# Separate random number streams -----------------------------------------------
#
# The hidden outbreak draws from its own random stream, so for a given seed
# every strategy faces the same outbreak (until its actions change the
# spread). Test results and other draws use the normal stream.

# Run `expr` using the saved stream `rng`; returns list(value, rng)
with_stream <- function(rng, expr) {
  outer <- get0(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  assign(".Random.seed", rng, envir = globalenv())

  value <- force(expr)

  rng_after <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  if (is.null(outer)) {
    rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  } else {
    assign(".Random.seed", outer, envir = globalenv())
  }
  list(value = value, rng = rng_after)
}

# A fresh stream started from a seed, without disturbing the current one
new_stream <- function(seed) {
  outer <- get0(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  set.seed(seed)
  rng <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  if (is.null(outer)) {
    rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  } else {
    assign(".Random.seed", outer, envir = globalenv())
  }
  rng
}

# Testing settings for one turn, with this game's hidden biases --------------

# The testing level the game is at now (one row of test_levels)
current_test_level <- function(state, config) {
  levels <- config$tp$test_levels
  levels[levels$level == state$test_level, ]
}

# Costs, delays and capacity now: the PCR level, and rapid tests if developed
test_setup <- function(state, config) {
  lvl <- current_test_level(state, config)
  build <- config$tp$build_testing
  rapid <- config$tp$rapid_tests
  ag_available <- isTRUE(state$rapid_available)
  rapid_left <- state$rapid_left %||% 0L

  capacity <- lvl$capacity
  if (state$build_left > 0) {
    capacity <- capacity * build$capacity_while_building
  }

  list(
    level = lvl$level,
    label = if (ag_available) paste(lvl$label, "+ rapid tests") else lvl$label,
    ag_available = ag_available,
    costs = list(ag = if (ag_available) rapid$ag_cost else 0, pcr = lvl$pcr_cost),
    delays = list(ag = 0L, pcr = lvl$pcr_delay),
    # PCR the labs can process, and rapid test kits available
    capacity = floor(capacity),
    ag_capacity = if (ag_available) floor(rapid$kits) else 0,
    # improving PCR
    building = state$build_left > 0,
    build_left = state$build_left,
    can_build = state$build_left == 0 && lvl$level < max(config$tp$test_levels$level),
    build_cost = build$cost,
    build_turns = build$turns,
    # developing rapid tests
    developing_rapid = rapid_left > 0,
    rapid_left = rapid_left,
    can_develop_rapid = !ag_available && rapid_left == 0,
    rapid_cost = rapid$cost,
    rapid_turns = rapid$turns
  )
}

# Antigen kits are limited by supply: scale antigen tests down to capacity,
# and drop them if they do not exist yet at this level. PCR is not capped
# here; beyond lab capacity it queues (see lab_backlog_delay()).
cap_to_capacity <- function(allocs, setup) {
  if (!setup$ag_available) {
    allocs$n_ag <- 0L
  }
  total_ag <- sum(allocs$n_ag)
  if (total_ag > setup$ag_capacity) {
    scale <- setup$ag_capacity / total_ag
    allocs$n_ag <- as.integer(floor(allocs$n_ag * scale))
  }
  allocs
}

# Lab backlog: labs process `capacity` PCR tests a turn. Tests waiting from
# earlier turns go first, so this turn's results are late by however many
# extra turns it takes to clear the queue in front of them.
lab_backlog_delay <- function(backlog_before, pcr_today, capacity) {
  extra_delay <- 0L
  if (pcr_today > 0) {
    extra_delay <- as.integer(floor((backlog_before + pcr_today - 1) / capacity))
  }
  list(
    extra_delay = extra_delay,
    backlog_after = max(0, backlog_before + pcr_today - capacity)
  )
}

# People still test-positive in each borough: infections over the last
# `window` turns (this turn included)
detectable_infections <- function(truth, window) {
  history <- truth$history
  recent <- utils::tail(history, window)
  Reduce(`+`, recent)
}

testing_for_turn <- function(state, config, sampling_mode = "symptomatic") {
  tests <- config$tp$tests
  setup <- test_setup(state, config)
  window <- config$tp$detection_window

  testing <- list(
    sens = tests$sens,
    spec = tests$spec,
    delays = setup$delays,
    prev_floor = tests$prev_floor,
    sampling_mode = sampling_mode,
    sampling_pool_frac = config$tp$symptomatic$pool_frac,
    detectable = list(
      ag = detectable_infections(state$truth, window$ag),
      pcr = detectable_infections(state$truth, window$pcr)
    )
  )

  # symptomatic testing is distorted by care-seeking and the illness wave
  if (identical(sampling_mode, "symptomatic") && !is.null(state$biases)) {
    testing$sampling_pool_frac <- symptomatic_pool_frac(state$turn, state$biases$wave_peak, config$tp)
    testing$care_seeking <- state$biases$care_seeking
    testing$symptomatic_share <- 1 - (config$bio$asymptomatic %||% 0)
  }

  testing
}

# Cases isolated this turn because their positive result came back.
# Only real infections count, discounted by how late the result was.
# With contact tracing on, each traced case also takes out some of the
# people it has already infected (about Rt of them), up to the tracers'
# capacity. Tracers follow up every positive, real or false.
isolated_from_results <- function(results, n_boroughs, tp, tracing = FALSE, Rt = 1, bio = list(),
                                  gens_per_turn = 1, admissions = NULL) {
  isolated <- numeric(n_boroughs)

  # contact tracing (if on): the infected contacts it finds are quarantined
  traced <- traced_contacts(results, n_boroughs, tp, Rt, bio, gens_per_turn, admissions)
  if (isTRUE(tracing)) {
    isolated <- isolated + traced$infected_by_borough
  }

  if (!is.null(results) && nrow(results) > 0) {
    # isolation is stretched when there are many positives to support
    strain <- 1 / (1 + sum(results$positives) / tp$isolation$half_strength_load)
    effective <- found_still_infectious(results, bio, gens_per_turn) * tp$isolation$effectiveness * strain

    by_boro <- tapply(effective, results$borough_index, sum)
    idx <- as.integer(names(by_boro))
    isolated[idx] <- isolated[idx] + by_boro
  }

  # what the tracers did, for the report (none if tracing is off)
  attr(isolated, "tracing") <- if (isTRUE(tracing)) traced[c("cases", "contacts", "infected", "in_time")] else NULL
  isolated
}

# Real, still-infectious cases among returned results, discounted by how late
# the result was (and, if found through symptoms, by the spread already done)
found_still_infectious <- function(results, bio, gens_per_turn) {
  delay <- results$turn_available - results$turn_sampled
  # delay_decay is per generation; a report's delay spans gens_per_turn of them
  timeliness <- (bio$delay_decay %||% 0.5)^(delay * gens_per_turn)

  found_by_symptoms <- !is.na(results$mode) & results$mode == "symptomatic"
  timeliness <- timeliness * ifelse(found_by_symptoms, 1 - (bio$presymptomatic %||% 0), 1)

  still_infectious <- results$infectious_pos
  if (is.null(still_infectious)) {
    still_infectious <- results$true_pos
  }
  still_infectious[is.na(still_infectious)] <- results$true_pos[is.na(still_infectious)]

  still_infectious * timeliness
}

# Contact tracing ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Tracers follow up every known case: each positive test (real or false) and
# each admission in the latest hospital report, up to their capacity. For
# each real case they reach, they find about Rt of the people it has already
# infected (an admission's contacts are discounted by how long ago it was
# infected). They also name and check contacts_per_case people per case,
# which is what the report shows.
traced_contacts <- function(results, n_boroughs, tp, Rt, bio, gens_per_turn, admissions) {
  trc <- tp$tracing
  admissions <- if (is.null(admissions)) numeric(n_boroughs) else admissions
  n_positives <- if (is.null(results)) 0 else sum(results$positives)
  known_cases <- n_positives + sum(admissions)

  # share of known cases the tracers can reach this report
  traced_share <- min(1, trc$capacity / max(1, known_cases))
  per_case <- traced_share * trc$effectiveness * Rt

  # `in_time`: infected contacts quarantined before they could pass it on
  # (what actually cuts spread); `found`: all infected contacts found
  in_time <- numeric(n_boroughs)
  found <- sum(admissions) * per_case

  # contacts of hospital cases: infected hosp_delay reports ago
  late <- (bio$delay_decay %||% 0.5)^((bio$hosp_delay %||% 1) * gens_per_turn)
  in_time <- in_time + admissions * per_case * late

  # contacts of real cases found by testing
  if (!is.null(results) && nrow(results) > 0) {
    caught <- found_still_infectious(results, bio, gens_per_turn) * per_case
    by_boro <- tapply(caught, results$borough_index, sum)
    idx <- as.integer(names(by_boro))
    in_time[idx] <- in_time[idx] + by_boro
    found <- found + sum(results$true_pos) * per_case
  }

  cases <- round(traced_share * known_cases)
  list(
    infected_by_borough = in_time,
    cases = cases,
    contacts = cases * (trc$contacts_per_case %||% 10),
    infected = round(max(found, sum(in_time))),
    in_time = round(sum(in_time))
  )
}

# The public health agency's steady sample (see teaching_params()$sentinel):
# the same number of people with symptoms tested every report, spread by
# population. Information only; returns tests and positives for this turn.
sentinel_sample <- function(state, config) {
  sen <- config$tp$sentinel
  if (is.null(sen) || is.null(sen$tests) || sen$tests <= 0) return(NULL)
  pop <- config$pop_tbl$pop
  allocs <- empty_allocations(config)
  allocs$n_pcr <- as.integer(floor(sen$tests * pop / sum(pop)))
  allocs <- cap_to_pool(allocs, symptomatic_pool_size(state, config))

  testing <- testing_for_turn(state, config, "symptomatic")
  testing$delays$pcr <- 0L
  testing$source <- "agency"
  obs <- observe_tests(init_observation_state(), state$turn, allocs, state$truth$incidence, config$pop_tbl, testing)
  data.frame(turn = as.integer(state$turn), tests = sum(obs$available$n), positives = sum(obs$available$positives))
}

# Admissions per borough in the latest hospital report
reported_admissions <- function(state, n_boroughs) {
  out <- numeric(n_boroughs)
  rep <- state$reports
  if (is.null(rep) || nrow(rep) == 0) {
    return(out)
  }
  latest <- rep[rep$turn == state$turn, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(latest) == 0) {
    return(out)
  }
  by_boro <- tapply(latest$admissions, latest$borough_index, sum)
  out[as.integer(names(by_boro))] <- by_boro
  out
}

# How many people come forward for a test in each borough this turn
symptomatic_pool_size <- function(state, config) {
  pool_frac <- symptomatic_pool_frac(state$turn, state$biases$wave_peak, config$tp)
  floor(config$pop_tbl$pop * pool_frac)
}

# Symptomatic testing can only test the people who come forward: scale the
# allocation down in any borough where it asks for more tests than that
cap_to_pool <- function(allocs, pool_size) {
  wanted <- allocs$n_ag + allocs$n_pcr
  scale <- ifelse(wanted > pool_size, pool_size / pmax(wanted, 1), 1)
  allocs$n_ag <- as.integer(floor(allocs$n_ag * scale))
  allocs$n_pcr <- as.integer(floor(allocs$n_pcr * scale))
  allocs
}

# Keep restricted areas, in the order chosen, while they hold at most
# max_pop_share of the population (the first area is always allowed)
within_restriction_limit <- function(restricted, config) {
  share <- config$tp$local_restrictions$max_pop_share
  if (is.null(share) || length(restricted) == 0) return(restricted)
  pop <- config$pop_tbl$pop
  covered <- cumsum(pop[restricted]) / sum(pop)
  restricted[covered <= share | seq_along(restricted) == 1]
}

# Per-turn cost of restricting each borough
local_restriction_costs <- function(config) {
  nice_round(config$tp$local_restrictions$cost_per_100k * config$pop_tbl$pop / 1e5)
}

# Effect of local restrictions this turn, given how long each borough has
# been restricted (streak, including this turn)
local_restriction_multiplier <- function(local_streaks, tp) {
  lr <- tp$local_restrictions
  strength <- vapply(local_streaks, intervention_strength, numeric(1), lag = lr$lag, fatigue = lr$fatigue)
  1 - strength * (1 - lr$Rt_multiplier)
}

# Hospitals (hidden truth) ----------------------------------------------------
#
# Admissions come from infections `hosp_delay` turns ago. Beds are a
# London-wide pool; patients stay `stay_turns`. Patients admitted when there
# is no bed for them die at an extra rate (added to the truth's deaths).
hospital_step <- function(truth, hospital, config) {
  hosp <- config$tp$hospital
  n_b <- nrow(config$pop_tbl)

  # infections that are now sick enough for hospital
  source_turn <- truth$turn - (config$bio$hosp_delay %||% config$tp$reports$hosp_delay)
  admitted <- integer(n_b)
  if (source_turn >= 0) {
    infected <- truth$history[[source_turn + 1]]
    admitted <- stats::rbinom(n_b, size = infected, prob = config$bio$hosp_frac)
  }

  # beds in use = everyone admitted over the last stay_turns turns
  admissions <- c(hospital$admissions, list(admitted))
  occupancy <- sum(unlist(utils::tail(admissions, hosp$stay_turns)))

  # share of patients without a proper bed, and the extra deaths that causes
  overload <- if (occupancy > hosp$beds) (occupancy - hosp$beds) / occupancy else 0
  extra_deaths <- stats::rbinom(n_b, size = admitted, prob = overload * hosp$death_if_no_bed)

  truth$deaths <- as.integer(truth$deaths + extra_deaths)
  truth$cumulative_deaths <- as.integer(truth$cumulative_deaths + extra_deaths)
  truth$death_history[[length(truth$death_history)]] <- truth$deaths

  list(
    truth = truth,
    hospital = list(
      admissions = admissions,
      occupancy = c(hospital$occupancy, occupancy),
      extra_deaths = c(hospital$extra_deaths, sum(extra_deaths))
    ),
    admitted = admitted,
    overload = overload
  )
}

# Hospital admissions and deaths reported this turn -----------------------------
#
# Hospitals report the admissions they record (fewer when they are full);
# most are reported in the patient's own borough, the rest at a neighbouring
# borough's hospital. They also publish how full they are.
draw_reports <- function(truth, config, admitted, overload = 0, offset = 0) {
  rep_par <- config$tp$reports
  n_b <- nrow(config$pop_tbl)
  turn_now <- truth$turn - offset

  ascertainment <- rep_par$hosp_ascertainment * (1 - config$tp$hospital$reporting_drop_when_full * overload)
  admissions_home <- stats::rbinom(n_b, size = admitted, prob = ascertainment)

  # where they are reported: own borough or a neighbour's hospital
  admissions <- integer(n_b)
  for (i in which(admissions_home > 0)) {
    at_home <- stats::rbinom(1, admissions_home[i], rep_par$own_borough)
    admissions[i] <- admissions[i] + at_home
    elsewhere <- admissions_home[i] - at_home
    neighbours <- which(config$A[i, ] > 0)
    if (elsewhere > 0 && length(neighbours) > 0) {
      dest <- neighbours[sample.int(length(neighbours), elsewhere, replace = TRUE)]
      admissions <- admissions + tabulate(dest, nbins = n_b)
    } else {
      admissions[i] <- admissions[i] + elsewhere
    }
  }

  deaths <- stats::rbinom(n_b, size = as.integer(truth$deaths), prob = rep_par$death_ascertainment)

  data.frame(
    turn = as.integer(turn_now),
    borough_index = seq_len(n_b),
    admissions = as.integer(admissions),
    deaths = as.integer(deaths)
  )
}

# Empty allocation table (no tests anywhere)
empty_allocations <- function(config) {
  n_b <- nrow(config$pop_tbl)
  data.frame(
    borough_index = seq_len(n_b),
    borough_name = config$pop_tbl$borough_name,
    n_ag = integer(n_b),
    n_pcr = integer(n_b),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Start a new game -------------------------------------------------------------

new_game <- function(config, seed = NULL, sampling_mode = "symptomatic") {
  if (is.null(seed)) {
    seed <- sample.int(1e6, 1)
  }
  set.seed(seed)

  n_b <- nrow(config$pop_tbl)
  epi <- config$epi

  # where the outbreak starts
  origin <- epi$seed_borough
  if (is.null(origin) || is.na(origin)) {
    origin <- sample.int(n_b, 1L)
  }

  # it runs unseen until a cluster of severe illness is noticed: enough
  # hospital admissions in total, or the first death
  hs <- config$tp$head_start
  gens_per_turn <- config$gens_per_turn %||% 1
  hosp_delay <- config$bio$hosp_delay %||% config$tp$reports$hosp_delay
  hosp_frac <- config$bio$hosp_frac %||% 0

  # the hidden outbreak's own random stream
  truth_rng <- new_stream(seed + 7919L)

  # run the hidden turns from one infected person (an outbreak that dies out
  # before anyone notices is never reported, so draw again)
  for (attempt in 1:50) {
    truth <- init_truth(n_boroughs = n_b, seed_boroughs = origin, seed_cases = hs$index_cases)
    admitted <- numeric(n_b)
    hidden_turns <- 0L

    trigger <- "none"
    for (i in seq_len(hs$max_reports)) {
      stepped <- with_stream(truth_rng, step_truth(
        state = truth,
        K = config$K,
        Rt_global = epi$Rt,
        k_overdisp = epi$k,
        imports_prob = epi$imports_prob,
        lambda_import = epi$lambda_import,
        pop = config$pop_tbl$pop,
        susceptible_frac = config$susceptible_frac,
        death_ifr = config$mort$death_ifr,
        death_delay = config$mort$death_delay,
        gens_per_step = gens_per_turn
      ))
      truth <- stepped$value
      truth_rng <- stepped$rng
      hidden_turns <- i

      # people infected hosp_delay reports ago who are now in hospital
      source_turn <- length(truth$history) - hosp_delay
      if (source_turn >= 1) {
        infected <- truth$history[[source_turn]]
        drawn <- with_stream(truth_rng, stats::rbinom(n_b, size = infected, prob = hosp_frac))
        admitted <- admitted + drawn$value
        truth_rng <- drawn$rng
      }

      # a death, or a cluster of admissions, is noticed: reported now
      if (sum(truth$cumulative_deaths) > 0) {
        trigger <- "death"
        break
      }
      if (sum(admitted) >= hs$admissions) {
        trigger <- "admissions"
        break
      }

      # died out unseen (nothing infectious, no deaths still to come)
      if (sum(truth$incidence) == 0 && sum(unlist(truth$death_queue)) == 0) {
        break
      }
    }

    if (trigger != "none") {
      break
    }
  }

  # if it kept dying out unseen (spread far below 1), the first report is a
  # single fresh spillover patient where it began
  if (trigger == "none") {
    trigger <- "admissions"
    admitted[origin] <- 1
    truth$incidence[origin] <- 1L
    truth$cumulative[origin] <- truth$cumulative[origin] + 1L
    truth$history[[length(truth$history)]] <- truth$incidence
  }

  # the first report comes from one area: where someone died, or the area
  # with the most admissions (ties broken at random). Not necessarily where
  # it began.
  report_counts <- if (trigger == "death") truth$cumulative_deaths else admitted
  top <- which(report_counts == max(report_counts))
  first_patient <- if (length(top) == 1) top else sample(top, 1L)

  state <- list(
    turn = 0L,
    truth = truth,
    # turns of hidden history before the game's turn 0
    truth_offset = hidden_turns,
    # infections and deaths already set in motion before the game began
    start_infections = sum(truth$cumulative),
    start_deaths_eventual = eventual_deaths(truth, config),
    start_deaths = sum(truth$cumulative_deaths),
    obs = init_observation_state(),
    available = init_observation_state()$history,
    biases = draw_game_biases(n_b, config$tp),
    streaks = integer(),
    local_streaks = integer(n_b),
    test_level = config$test_level,
    build_left = 0L,
    rapid_left = 0L,
    rapid_available = FALSE,
    sentinel = data.frame(turn = integer(), tests = integer(), positives = integer()),
    lab_backlog = 0,
    reports = data.frame(turn = integer(), borough_index = integer(), admissions = integer(), deaths = integer()),
    hospital = list(admissions = list(), occupancy = numeric(), extra_deaths = numeric()),
    spend_total = 0,
    alert = list(
      alerted = first_patient,
      true_start = origin,
      hidden_turns = hidden_turns,
      trigger = trigger,
      admissions = sum(admitted)
    ),
    seed = seed,
    truth_rng = truth_rng
  )

  # no free tests: the first report is one patient, nothing more
  state$starter_alloc <- empty_allocations(config)
  state
}

# Deaths so far plus deaths still to come from people already infected
eventual_deaths <- function(truth, config) {
  in_pipeline <- sum(unlist(truth$death_queue))
  sum(truth$cumulative_deaths) + in_pipeline * config$mort$death_ifr
}

# Compare a finished game with doing nothing ------------------------------------
#
# Replays the same outbreak (same seed, so the same hidden start and the same
# random spread until actions change it) for the same number of reports with
# no response, and counts infections and deaths during the response in both.
# Deaths include those already set in motion (eventual deaths).
compare_with_doing_nothing <- function(state, config) {
  nothing <- new_game(config, seed = state$seed)
  for (i in seq_len(state$turn)) {
    nothing <- play_turn(nothing, list(), config)$state
  }

  during <- function(s) {
    list(
      infections = sum(s$truth$cumulative) - (s$start_infections %||% 0),
      deaths = max(0, eventual_deaths(s$truth, config) - (s$start_deaths_eventual %||% 0))
    )
  }
  you <- during(state)
  none <- during(nothing)

  # share prevented (negative = worse than doing nothing)
  prevented <- function(a, b) if (b > 0) 1 - a / b else NA_real_

  list(
    infections = you$infections,
    infections_doing_nothing = none$infections,
    deaths = you$deaths,
    deaths_doing_nothing = none$deaths,
    infections_prevented = prevented(you$infections, none$infections),
    deaths_prevented = prevented(you$deaths, none$deaths)
  )
}

# Is the outbreak declared over? True after declare_over_after reports in a
# row with no hospital admissions and no deaths reported (public data only).
declared_over <- function(state, config) {
  quiet_needed <- config$tp$declare_over_after
  if (is.null(quiet_needed) || state$turn < quiet_needed) return(FALSE)
  rep <- state$reports
  recent <- rep[rep$turn > state$turn - quiet_needed, , drop = FALSE]
  sum(recent$admissions) + sum(recent$deaths) == 0
}

# Would people accept a lockdown? Only after enough reported deaths, or with
# hospitals filling up (both public).
lockdown_allowed <- function(state, config) {
  trigger <- config$tp$lockdown_trigger
  if (is.null(trigger)) return(TRUE)
  deaths_reported <- if (is.null(state$reports)) 0 else sum(state$reports$deaths)
  occupancy <- state$hospital$occupancy
  bed_share <- if (length(occupancy) == 0) 0 else utils::tail(occupancy, 1) / config$tp$hospital$beds
  deaths_reported >= trigger$deaths || bed_share >= trigger$bed_share
}

# Play one turn ----------------------------------------------------------------
#
# actions: list with
#   allocations   tibble of n_ag / n_pcr per borough (default: none)
#   sampling_mode "symptomatic" or "random"
#   interventions character vector of intervention ids
#
# Returns list(ok, state, ...). If the actions cost more than the budget,
# ok is FALSE and the state is unchanged.

play_turn <- function(state, actions, config) {
  tp <- config$tp

  allocs <- actions$allocations %||% empty_allocations(config)
  sampling_mode <- actions$sampling_mode %||% "symptomatic"
  selected <- actions$interventions %||% character()
  # no lockdown until people would accept one
  if (!lockdown_allowed(state, config)) {
    selected <- setdiff(selected, "distancing")
  }
  restricted <- unique(as.integer(actions$local_restrictions %||% integer()))
  restricted <- within_restriction_limit(restricted, config)
  tracing <- isTRUE(actions$tracing)
  n_b <- nrow(config$pop_tbl)

  # testing level, costs and capacity this turn
  setup <- test_setup(state, config)
  start_build <- isTRUE(actions$build_testing) && setup$can_build
  build_cost <- if (start_build) setup$build_cost else 0
  if (start_build) {
    # capacity drops straight away while staff are diverted
    setup <- test_setup(modifyList(state, list(build_left = setup$build_turns)), config)
  }
  # rapid tests are paid for every report while they are being developed
  start_rapid <- isTRUE(actions$develop_rapid) && setup$can_develop_rapid
  rapid_cost <- if (start_rapid || setup$developing_rapid) setup$rapid_cost else 0
  allocs <- cap_to_capacity(allocs, setup)

  # symptomatic testing is limited to the people who come forward
  if (identical(sampling_mode, "symptomatic")) {
    allocs <- cap_to_pool(allocs, symptomatic_pool_size(state, config))
  }

  # local restrictions: per-borough streaks give lag and fatigue
  # restrictions fade the longer they run; once lifted, that fading wears
  # off one report per report (so switching off for a week is no reset)
  local_streaks <- ifelse(seq_len(n_b) %in% restricted, state$local_streaks + 1L,
                          pmax(0L, state$local_streaks - 1L))
  local_mult <- local_restriction_multiplier(local_streaks, tp)
  local_cost <- sum(local_restriction_costs(config)[restricted])

  # interventions: lag and fatigue depend on how long each has been on
  streaks <- update_intervention_streaks(state$streaks, selected, config$interventions)
  # with rapid tests people can test at home and isolate, so a lockdown works better
  catalog <- config$interventions
  if (isTRUE(state$rapid_available) && !is.null(tp$rapid_tests$lockdown_Rt_multiplier)) {
    catalog$Rt_multiplier[catalog$id == "distancing"] <- tp$rapid_tests$lockdown_Rt_multiplier
  }
  effects <- compute_intervention_effects(selected, catalog, streaks = streaks)

  # spend this turn: capped per turn and by what is left in the pot
  budget <- min(tp$tests$budget, tp$budget_total - state$spend_total)
  spend_stats <- summarise_budget(allocs, setup$costs, budget)
  tracing_cost <- if (tracing) tp$tracing$cost else 0
  turn_spend <- spend_stats$spend + effects$cost + local_cost + tracing_cost + build_cost + rapid_cost
  if (turn_spend > budget + 1e-6) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, reason = "over_budget", state = state))
  }

  # testing this turn (interventions can shorten delays)
  testing <- testing_for_turn(state, config, sampling_mode)
  testing$delays$ag <- max(0, testing$delays$ag + effects$delay_adjust$ag)
  testing$delays$pcr <- max(0, testing$delays$pcr + effects$delay_adjust$pcr)

  # PCR beyond lab capacity waits in a backlog, making results later
  backlog <- lab_backlog_delay(state$lab_backlog %||% 0, sum(allocs$n_pcr), setup$capacity)
  testing$delays$pcr <- testing$delays$pcr + backlog$extra_delay

  obs <- observe_tests(
    state = state$obs,
    turn = state$turn,
    allocations = allocs,
    truth_incidence = state$truth$incidence,
    pop_tbl = config$pop_tbl,
    params = testing
  )

  # cases found this turn are isolated (and traced) before they pass it on
  isolated <- isolated_from_results(
    obs$available, n_b, tp,
    tracing = tracing,
    # each case's onward infections by the next report: effective R
    # (immunity included, not R0), compounded over the report's generations
    Rt = (config$epi$Rt * effects$Rt_multiplier * config$susceptible_frac)^(config$gens_per_turn %||% 1),
    bio = config$bio,
    gens_per_turn = config$gens_per_turn %||% 1,
    # admissions hospitals reported in the latest report (where the hospital is)
    admissions = reported_admissions(state, n_b)
  )
  if (!is.null(state$carry_isolated)) {
    isolated <- isolated + state$carry_isolated
  }

  # hidden outbreak moves on one turn
  epi <- config$epi
  stepped <- with_stream(state$truth_rng, step_truth(
    state = state$truth,
    K = config$K,
    Rt_global = epi$Rt * effects$Rt_multiplier,
    k_overdisp = epi$k,
    imports_prob = min(1, max(0, epi$imports_prob * effects$imports_multiplier)),
    lambda_import = epi$lambda_import,
    pop = config$pop_tbl$pop,
    susceptible_frac = config$susceptible_frac,
    death_ifr = config$mort$death_ifr,
    death_delay = config$mort$death_delay,
    isolated = isolated,
    local_multiplier = local_mult,
    gens_per_step = config$gens_per_turn %||% 1
  ))
  next_truth <- stepped$value

  # hospitals fill up (hidden), on the outbreak's own random stream
  hospital_now <- with_stream(stepped$rng, hospital_step(next_truth, state$hospital, config))
  next_truth <- hospital_now$value$truth

  # label shows how strong each intervention was this turn
  intervention_label <- if (length(effects$labels) == 0) {
    "None"
  } else {
    paste0(effects$labels, " (", round(100 * effects$strength), "%)", collapse = ", ")
  }

  new_state <- state
  new_state$turn <- state$turn + 1L
  new_state$truth <- next_truth
  new_state$truth_rng <- hospital_now$rng
  new_state$hospital <- hospital_now$value$hospital

  # what hospitals and death registrations report this turn
  new_state$reports <- rbind(
    state$reports,
    draw_reports(next_truth, config, hospital_now$value$admitted, hospital_now$value$overload,
                 offset = state$truth_offset %||% 0)
  )
  new_state$carry_isolated <- NULL
  # the agency's sample this report (comes back with the next report)
  new_state$sentinel <- rbind(state$sentinel, sentinel_sample(state, config))
  new_state$tracing_report <- attr(isolated, "tracing")
  new_state$obs <- list(queue = obs$queue, history = obs$history)
  new_state$available <- obs$available
  new_state$streaks <- streaks
  new_state$local_streaks <- local_streaks

  # building better testing: counts down, then moves up a level
  build_left <- if (start_build) setup$build_turns else state$build_left
  if (build_left > 0) {
    build_left <- build_left - 1L
    if (build_left == 0L) {
      new_state$test_level <- state$test_level + 1L
    }
  }
  new_state$build_left <- build_left

  # developing rapid tests: counts down, then they exist
  rapid_left <- if (start_rapid) setup$rapid_turns else (state$rapid_left %||% 0L)
  if (rapid_left > 0) {
    rapid_left <- rapid_left - 1L
    if (rapid_left == 0L) {
      new_state$rapid_available <- TRUE
    }
  }
  new_state$rapid_left <- rapid_left
  new_state$lab_backlog <- backlog$backlog_after
  new_state$spend_total <- state$spend_total + turn_spend

  list(
    ok = TRUE,
    state = new_state,
    turn_played = state$turn,
    allocations = allocs,
    available = obs$available,
    queue = obs$queue,
    allocation_spend = spend_stats$spend,
    intervention_cost = effects$cost,
    local_cost = local_cost,
    tracing_cost = tracing_cost,
    build_cost = build_cost,
    rapid_cost = rapid_cost,
    test_level = new_state$test_level,
    pcr_extra_delay = backlog$extra_delay,
    restricted = restricted,
    turn_spend = turn_spend,
    remaining = budget - turn_spend,
    tracing_report = attr(isolated, "tracing"),
    effects = effects,
    intervention_label = intervention_label,
    Rt_used = epi$Rt * effects$Rt_multiplier
  )
}

# What a player is allowed to see ---------------------------------------------
#
# Only results that have come back, how many tests are still pending (not
# their results), money, and public facts about the boroughs and tests.

player_view <- function(state, config) {
  tp <- config$tp

  # returned results only, without the hidden columns
  history <- state$obs$history[, c("borough_index", "borough_name", "type", "n", "positives",
                                   "turn_sampled", "turn_available"), drop = FALSE]

  # tests still at the lab, by type (not their results)
  queue <- state$obs$queue
  pending <- if (nrow(queue) == 0) {
    data.frame(type = character(), n = integer(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    waiting <- tapply(queue$n, queue$type, sum)
    data.frame(type = names(waiting), n = as.integer(waiting), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  # test setup once (it is used three times below)
  setup <- test_setup(state, config)

  # money left, and a fair share of it per remaining turn
  budget_left <- tp$budget_total - state$spend_total
  turns_left <- max(1, tp$game_turns - state$turn)

  list(
    turn = state$turn,
    turns_left = turns_left,
    history = history,
    pending = pending,
    budget = min(tp$tests$budget, budget_left),
    budget_left = budget_left,
    allowance = min(tp$tests$budget, budget_left / turns_left),
    spend_total = state$spend_total,
    testing = setup,
    costs = setup$costs,
    sens = tp$tests$sens,
    spec = tp$tests$spec,
    delays = setup$delays,
    interventions = config$interventions,
    streaks = state$streaks,
    local_costs = local_restriction_costs(config),
    tracing_cost = tp$tracing$cost,
    # labs publish their backlog (PCR tests waiting to be processed)
    lab_backlog = state$lab_backlog %||% 0,
    # how many people came forward for a test this turn (public: test demand)
    pool_size = symptomatic_pool_size(state, config),
    local_streaks = state$local_streaks,
    lockdown_allowed = lockdown_allowed(state, config),
    restriction_share = tp$local_restrictions$max_pop_share,
    # the public health agency's steady sample (public)
    sentinel = state$sentinel,
    alerted = if (is.null(state$alert)) NA_integer_ else state$alert$alerted,
    reports = state$reports,
    # hospitals publish how full they are (share of beds in use)
    bed_pressure = if (length(state$hospital$occupancy) == 0) 0 else
      utils::tail(state$hospital$occupancy, 1) / tp$hospital$beds,
    pop_tbl = config$pop_tbl,
    A = config$A
  )
}

# Help modal -----------------------------------------------------------------

help_modal_body <- function(scenario_id = NULL, scenario_defs = scenario_catalog(), show_scenario = TRUE) {
  if (is.null(scenario_id) || is.na(scenario_id) || scenario_id == "") {
    scenario_id <- "custom"
  }

  current <- scenario_lookup(scenario_id, scenario_defs)
  current_label <- current$label[[1]]
  current_objective <- current$objective[[1]]

  shiny::tagList(
    shiny::tags$h5("How to play"),
    shiny::tags$ol(
      shiny::tags$li("Set your response below the map: who to test, where, which test and how much to spend, plus any control measures."),
      shiny::tags$li("Press Next report. Your plan carries on each report until you change it."),
      shiny::tags$li("Read what came back: positives, tests, hospital reports. Ask what they really tell you."),
      shiny::tags$li(sprintf("When time runs out (after %d reports, or earlier) press End & review to see what really happened, then Replay this outbreak (in the Game menu) to try another strategy.", teaching_params()$game_turns))
    ),
    shiny::tags$details(
      shiny::tags$summary("More detail"),
    shiny::tags$p(
      "Your goal is to allocate testing under budget and delay constraints",
      "to infer how the outbreak is evolving, then compare those inferences",
      "with the truth reveal. You can delegate specific tests to chosen",
      "boroughs manually, or use mass testing so the remaining budget is",
      "spread evenly across boroughs."
    ),
    shiny::tags$p(
      "Set your response below the map: who to test (people with symptoms,",
      "or a random sample of residents), where (everywhere, boroughs with",
      "positive results so far, or boroughs you choose by clicking the map),",
      "which test, and how much to spend each turn. The plan carries on each",
      "turn until you change it. Switch the map to Restrict a borough to put",
      "local restrictions on a borough. You can also use London-wide Social",
      "distancing (lower Rt), Contact tracing (follows up your positives and",
      "the cases hospitals report), and Build better testing (faster,",
      "cheaper tests after a few turns, at half capacity meanwhile). Measures",
      "are charged every turn until switched off, only start working the turn",
      "after you switch them on, and some lose effect the longer they run. You",
      "have one budget for the whole outbreak. Hospital admissions, deaths, how",
      "full hospitals are and the lab backlog are reported whatever you do,",
      "but admissions are late and not always where the patient lives.",
      "Use the questions below as a guide for interpreting what you see and",
      "comparing it with the replay."
    ),
    ),
    shiny::tags$h5("Current scenario"),
    if (isTRUE(show_scenario)) {
      shiny::tags$div(
        class = "mb-3",
        shiny::tags$div(shiny::tags$strong(current_label)),
        if (!is.null(current_objective) && !is.na(current_objective) &&
            !identical(current_objective, "")) {
          shiny::tags$div(class = "text-muted small", current_objective)
        }
      )
    } else {
      shiny::tags$div(
        class = "mb-3 text-muted",
        "Hidden. Part of your job is to work out what kind of outbreak this is from the data."
      )
    },
    shiny::tags$h5("Be careful: the data can mislead you"),
    shiny::tags$ul(
      shiny::tags$li("Early alerts are not always right."),
      shiny::tags$li("A cheap test that is slightly wrong, used on many uninfected people, produces a lot of false positives."),
      shiny::tags$li("Symptomatic testing finds more cases, but who comes forward for a test, and what else is making people ill, both change what you see."),
      shiny::tags$li("Money spent on interventions is money not spent on seeing the outbreak.")
    ),
    shiny::tags$hr(),
    shiny::tags$h5("What you might think of during play"),
    shiny::tags$ul(
      shiny::tags$li("How is your testing strategy evolving (targeted vs broad, PCR vs antigen), and why?"),
      shiny::tags$li("What do observed positivity and the estimated Rt suggest about the trajectory, given delays?"),
      shiny::tags$li("Where do results appear on the map, and what might be missing or delayed?")
    ),
    shiny::tags$h5("Reflective questions after reveal"),
    shiny::tags$ul(
      shiny::tags$li("How does observed positivity compare with true prevalence in the replay?"),
      shiny::tags$li("When did sampling bias or delays distort your inference?"),
      shiny::tags$li("Which of your 'hotspots' were real, and which were false positives or a borough that tests more?"),
      shiny::tags$li("Did positivity fall because infections fell, or because more uninfected people were being tested?"),
      shiny::tags$li("What general testing strategy would you adjust next time?")
    )
  )
}

# Location picker module ------------------------------------------------------
#
# Free-text "Choose country or city" box. The best match is loaded from the
# prebuilt place library (prepare_place_library.R) and shown on a map:
#   - surrounding area in grey (context, not in play)
#   - units in play coloured by population, with names on hover
# The server returns a reactive with the chosen place:
#   list(meta = ..., inputs = <load_inputs()-shaped bundle>, context = ...)
# so the game can later run on `place()$inputs` instead of data/.
#
# Self-contained: not wired into app.R yet.


mod_location_picker_ui <- function(id, default_query = "London") {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)
  bslib::card(
    full_screen = TRUE,
    bslib::card_header("Choose where the outbreak happens"),
    shiny::div(
      class = "d-flex gap-2 align-items-end flex-wrap",
      shiny::textInput(
        ns("query"),
        label = "Choose country or city",
        value = default_query,
        placeholder = "e.g. Kenya, Lisbon, New York",
        width = "320px"
      ),
      shiny::actionButton(ns("go"), "Set up", class = "btn-primary mb-3")
    ),
    shiny::uiOutput(ns("matches")),
    shiny::div(class = "fw-semibold", shiny::textOutput(ns("summary"))),
    leaflet::leafletOutput(ns("map"), height = "480px"),
    shiny::div(
      class = "small text-muted mt-1",
      "Boundaries: geoBoundaries (licence varies by country, see docs/DATA_SOURCES.md); ",
      "population: GHS-POP 2020 (EC JRC, CC BY 4.0); Natural Earth."
    )
  )
}


mod_location_picker_server <- function(id,
                                       library_dir = file.path("locations", "library"),
                                       data_dir = "data") {
  shiny::moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    ns <- session$ns

    index <- read_place_index(library_dir)

    # ---- search: runs on "Set up" (and once at start) ----
    search_text <- shiny::reactiveVal(NULL)

    shiny::observeEvent(input$go, {
      search_text(input$query)
    }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

    hits <- shiny::reactive({
      shiny::req(search_text())
      find_place(search_text(), index, n = 6)
    })

    # Other matches, best one pre-selected (e.g. Hyderabad, India vs Pakistan)
    output$matches <- shiny::renderUI({
      found <- hits()
      if (nrow(found) == 0) {
        return(shiny::div(class = "text-danger mb-2",
                          paste0("No place called '", search_text(), "'. Try a country or a big city.")))
      }
      if (nrow(found) == 1) {
        return(NULL)
      }
      shiny::radioButtons(
        ns("place_id"),
        label = "Did you mean:",
        choices = stats::setNames(found$id, found$label),
        selected = found$id[1],
        inline = TRUE
      )
    })

    # ---- the chosen place ----
    chosen_id <- shiny::reactive({
      found <- hits()
      shiny::req(nrow(found) > 0)
      if (nrow(found) == 1 || is.null(input$place_id) || !input$place_id %in% found$id) {
        found$id[1]
      } else {
        input$place_id
      }
    })

    place <- shiny::reactive({
      load_place(chosen_id(), index, library_dir = library_dir, data_dir = data_dir)
    })

    output$summary <- shiny::renderText({
      p <- place()
      n_units <- nrow(p$inputs$pop_tbl)
      pop_total <- sum(p$inputs$pop_tbl$pop)
      unit_word <- if (p$meta$type == "city") "local areas" else "regions"
      sprintf("%s: %d %s in play (%s), %s people",
              p$meta$label, n_units, unit_word, p$meta$level,
              format(round(pop_total), big.mark = ","))
    })

    # ---- map ----
    output$map <- leaflet::renderLeaflet({
      p <- place()
      units <- p$inputs$boros
      context <- p$context

      pop_palette <- leaflet::colorNumeric(c("#FEE8C8", "#FDBB84", "#E34A33", "#7F0000"),
                                           domain = log10(units$pop))
      unit_labels <- sprintf("%s: %s people", units$borough_name,
                             format(round(units$pop), big.mark = ","))
      # Zoom to the units in play, with a margin so the surroundings show
      bbox <- sf::st_bbox(units)
      margin_x <- (bbox[["xmax"]] - bbox[["xmin"]]) * 0.15
      margin_y <- (bbox[["ymax"]] - bbox[["ymin"]]) * 0.15

      context_label <- if ("shapeName" %in% names(context)) context$shapeName else context$name

      # No web basemap: the grey surrounding units are the backdrop, so the
      # map works offline (and needs no tile-provider API key)
      leaflet::leaflet(options = leaflet::leafletOptions(zoomSnap = 0.25)) |>
        htmlwidgets::onRender("function(el) { el.style.background = '#DCEBF5'; }") |>
        # Surrounding area: grey, not in play
        leaflet::addPolygons(
          data = context,
          fillColor = "#BDBDBD", fillOpacity = 0.35,
          color = "#9E9E9E", weight = 0.6,
          label = context_label,
          group = "Surrounding area"
        ) |>
        # Units in play: coloured by population
        leaflet::addPolygons(
          data = units,
          fillColor = pop_palette(log10(units$pop)), fillOpacity = 0.75,
          color = "#3F3F3F", weight = 1,
          label = unit_labels,
          highlightOptions = leaflet::highlightOptions(weight = 3, color = "#000000", bringToFront = TRUE),
          group = "In play"
        ) |>
        leaflet::addLegend(
          position = "bottomright",
          colors = c("#E34A33", "#BDBDBD"),
          labels = c("In play (darker = more people)", "Surrounding area"),
          opacity = 0.8
        ) |>
        leaflet::fitBounds(bbox[["xmin"]] - margin_x, bbox[["ymin"]] - margin_y,
                           bbox[["xmax"]] + margin_x, bbox[["ymax"]] + margin_y)
    })

    place
  })
}

# Map module ----------------------------------------------------------------- # # Two pieces of UI share one server: # mod_map_ui() - the situation map (results, chosen and restricted areas) # mod_response_ui() - the response: who/where/which test/how much, control # measures, and what clicking the map does # The plan carries over from turn to turn until changed. # Map layers ------------------------------------------------------------------- # # Three public views of the latest report, one value per map area (in the # map's order). Colours come in fixed steps that never rescale, so the map # gets deeper and redder only as things really get worse. map_palette <- c("#a9c5d6", "#d9e6a1", "#f6d55c", "#f5a742", "#f28e2b", "#e15759", "#b8333f", "#7a1426") map_layers <- function(results, reports, pop_tbl, area_names) { n <- length(area_names) pop <- pop_tbl$pop[match(area_names, pop_tbl$borough_name)] # tests positive among results back this report tests <- numeric(n) positives <- numeric(n) if (!is.null(results) && nrow(results) > 0) { idx <- match(results$borough_name, area_names) tests <- as.numeric(tabulate_sum(idx, results$n, n)) positives <- as.numeric(tabulate_sum(idx, results$positives, n)) } positivity <- ifelse(tests > 0, positives / tests, NA_real_) # hospital admissions and deaths in the latest report, per 100,000 people admissions <- numeric(n) deaths <- numeric(n) if (!is.null(reports) && nrow(reports) > 0) { latest <- reports[reports$turn == max(reports$turn), , drop = FALSE] idx <- match(pop_tbl$borough_name[latest$borough_index], area_names) admissions <- as.numeric(tabulate_sum(idx, latest$admissions, n)) deaths <- as.numeric(tabulate_sum(idx, latest$deaths, n)) } per_100k <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, 1e5 * x / pop, NA_real_) rate_breaks <- c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100) rate_labels <- c("under 0.1", "0.1 to 0.3", "0.3 to 1", "1 to 3", "3 to 10", "10 to 30", "30 to 100", "100 or more") list( positivity = list( values = positivity, tests = tests, breaks = c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2), step_labels = c("under 0.1%", "0.1 to 0.5%", "0.5 to 1%", "1 to 2%", "2 to 5%", "5 to 10%", "10 to 20%", "20% or more"), none_label = "no results", title = "Tests positive
(results back
this report)" ), admissions = list( values = per_100k(admissions), counts = admissions, breaks = rate_breaks, step_labels = rate_labels, none_label = "none reported", title = "Hospital admissions
per 100,000
(this report)" ), deaths = list( values = per_100k(deaths), counts = deaths, breaks = rate_breaks, step_labels = rate_labels, none_label = "none reported", title = "Deaths
per 100,000
(this report)" ) ) } # sum `x` into `n` bins by index (NA indices dropped) tabulate_sum <- function(idx, x, n) { out <- numeric(n) keep <- !is.na(idx) if (any(keep)) { sums <- rowsum(x[keep], idx[keep]) out[as.integer(rownames(sums))] <- sums[, 1] } out } # colour for each value: its step on the fixed scale; NA = dark slate map_colours <- function(values, breaks) { step <- findInterval(values, breaks) + 1L ifelse(is.na(values), "#3d4f61", map_palette[pmin(step, length(map_palette))]) } mod_map_ui <- function(id, intervention_defs = intervention_catalog()) { ns <- shiny::NS(id) bslib::card( full_screen = TRUE, bslib::card_header( class = "d-flex align-items-center gap-3", "Situation map", shiny::div( class = "small ms-auto map-layer-switch", shiny::radioButtons( ns("map_layer"), label = NULL, inline = TRUE, choices = c("Tests positive" = "positivity", "Hospital admissions" = "admissions", "Deaths" = "deaths"), selected = "positivity" ) ) ), leaflet::leafletOutput(ns("map"), height = "400px"), shiny::div(class = "small text-muted mt-1", shiny::textOutput(ns("turn_positivity"), inline = TRUE)) ) } mod_response_ui <- function(id, intervention_defs = intervention_catalog()) { ns <- shiny::NS(id) tp <- teaching_params() bslib::card( bslib::card_header("Response"), bslib::layout_columns( col_widths = bslib::breakpoints(sm = c(12, 12, 12, 12), lg = c(3, 3, 4, 2)), fill = FALSE, # testing: who and where shiny::div( class = "small", # every real case a test finds is told to isolate shiny::radioButtons( ns("who"), label = "Test and isolate", choiceNames = list( shiny::HTML("People with symptoms (those who come forward ill; most have something else)"), shiny::HTML("A random sample (anyone, ill or not)") ), choiceValues = list("symptomatic", "random"), selected = "symptomatic" ), shiny::radioButtons( ns("where"), label = "Where", choices = c( "Everywhere" = "everywhere", "Where positives were found" = "positives", "Areas I pick on the map" = "chosen" ), selected = "everywhere" ) ), # testing: which test and how much shiny::div( class = "small", # built by the server each report (prices, waits, antigen greyed # out until it exists) shiny::uiOutput(ns("test_type_ui")), shiny::sliderInput( ns("spend"), label = paste0("Spend on tests (", tp$currency, " per report)"), min = 0, max = tp$tests$budget, value = 0, step = 5000, ticks = FALSE, sep = "," ), shiny::div(class = "text-muted", shiny::textOutput(ns("allocation_summary"), inline = TRUE)) ), # control measures and what they will do next shiny::div( class = "small", shiny::tags$label(class = "form-label", paste0("Measures (", tp$currency, " per report)")), # built by the server each report (prices; lockdown greyed out until # people would accept it) shiny::uiOutput(ns("interventions_ui")), shiny::checkboxInput(ns("tracing"), "Contact tracing", value = FALSE), shiny::checkboxInput(ns("build_testing"), "Improve PCR", value = FALSE), shiny::checkboxInput(ns("develop_rapid"), "Develop rapid tests", value = FALSE), shiny::div(class = "text-muted", shiny::htmlOutput(ns("measure_status"))) ), # what clicking the map does shiny::div( class = "small", shiny::radioButtons( ns("click_mode"), label = "Map click", choices = c("Pick test areas" = "choose", "Restrict an area" = "restrict"), selected = "choose" ) ) ) ) } mod_map_server <- function( id, boros, allocations_init, budget_info, observed_this_turn, observed_history = shiny::reactive(NULL), pop_tbl, app_ready = shiny::reactive(TRUE), intervention_defs = intervention_catalog(), first_report = shiny::reactive(NULL), reports = shiny::reactive(NULL)) { shiny::moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) { ns <- session$ns ready <- shiny::reactive({ isTRUE(app_ready()) }) map_ready <- shiny::reactiveVal(FALSE) observeEvent(input$map_bounds, { if (!is.null(input$map_bounds)) { map_ready(TRUE) } }) chosen <- shiny::reactiveVal(integer()) restricted <- shiny::reactiveVal(integer()) selected_interventions <- shiny::reactive({ sel <- input$interventions if (is.null(sel)) character() else sel }) # everything planned this turn apart from tests: interventions, local # restrictions, tracing and building testing other_cost <- function(restricted_now = restricted()) { budget <- budget_info() interventions <- compute_intervention_effects(selected_interventions(), intervention_defs)$cost local <- sum(budget$local_costs[restricted_now]) tracing <- if (isTRUE(input$tracing)) budget$tracing_cost else 0 build <- if (isTRUE(input$build_testing) && isTRUE(budget$testing$can_build)) budget$testing$build_cost else 0 # rapid tests: paid every report while being developed developing <- isTRUE(budget$testing$developing_rapid) || (isTRUE(input$develop_rapid) && isTRUE(budget$testing$can_develop_rapid)) build <- build + if (developing) budget$testing$rapid_cost else 0 interventions + local + tracing + build } # boroughs that have had at least one positive result returned so far positive_boroughs <- shiny::reactive({ hist <- observed_history() if (is.null(hist) || nrow(hist) == 0) { return(integer()) } sort(unique(hist$borough_index[hist$positives > 0])) }) # turn the testing plan into tests per borough --------------------------- plan <- shiny::reactive({ budget <- budget_info() # test type (PCR if antigen does not exist yet) test <- input$test_type %||% "pcr" if (test == "ag" && !isTRUE(budget$testing$ag_available)) { test <- "pcr" } cost <- budget$costs[[test]] # which boroughs where <- input$where %||% "everywhere" targets <- switch( where, everywhere = seq_len(nrow(pop_tbl)), positives = positive_boroughs(), chosen = chosen() ) # money: what the student asked for, cut down to what is left this turn asked <- input$spend %||% 0 money <- max(0, min(asked, budget$budget - other_cost())) n_tests <- if (length(targets) == 0 || cost <= 0) 0 else floor(money / cost) # spread the tests over the chosen boroughs by population per_borough <- integer(nrow(pop_tbl)) if (n_tests > 0) { per_borough[targets] <- spread_tests(n_tests, pop_tbl$pop[targets]) } allocs <- allocations_init if (test == "ag") { allocs$n_ag <- as.integer(per_borough) } else { allocs$n_pcr <- as.integer(per_borough) } list( allocations = allocs, test = test, where = where, targets = targets, asked = asked, money = money, cut_down = money < asked - 1e-6 ) }) # Compute borough centroids for allocation markers centroids <- sf::st_geometry(boros) |> sf::st_centroid(of_largest_polygon = TRUE) |> sf::st_coordinates() centroid_tbl <- tibble::tibble( borough_name = boros$borough_name, lng = centroids[, 1], lat = centroids[, 2] ) bbox <- sf::st_bbox(boros) # a margin of 10% of the place's size (London or a whole country) pad_x <- 0.1 * (bbox[["xmax"]] - bbox[["xmin"]]) pad_y <- 0.1 * (bbox[["ymax"]] - bbox[["ymin"]]) bounds_list <- list( c(bbox[["ymin"]] - pad_y, bbox[["xmin"]] - pad_x), c(bbox[["ymax"]] + pad_y, bbox[["xmax"]] + pad_x) ) reset_js <- sprintf( "function(btn, map){ map.fitBounds([[%.6f, %.6f],[%.6f, %.6f]]); }", bounds_list[[1]][1], bounds_list[[1]][2], bounds_list[[2]][1], bounds_list[[2]][2] ) output$map <- leaflet::renderLeaflet({ leaflet::leaflet( boros, options = leaflet::leafletOptions( # keep the view on the place, at whatever zoom fits it maxBounds = bounds_list, # the mouse wheel scrolls the page; zoom with the +/- buttons scrollWheelZoom = FALSE ) ) |> leaflet::addPolygons( layerId = boros$borough_name, weight = 0.8, color = "#ffffff", opacity = 0.8, fillOpacity = 0.9, fillColor = "#3d4f61", label = ~borough_name, group = "boroughs", highlight = leaflet::highlightOptions(weight = 2, bringToFront = TRUE) ) |> leaflet::addEasyButton( leaflet::easyButton( icon = "fa-home", title = "Reset view", onClick = htmlwidgets::JS(reset_js) ) ) |> # colour = share of tests positive among results back this turn # (the positivity legend is added with each update, so its scale can # follow this turn's results) leaflet::addControl( html = paste0( "
", " no results this report
", " restricted
", " chosen for testing
", " first report's area (lit until tested)", "
first report", "
" ), position = "bottomleft" ) |> leaflet::fitBounds( lng1 = bbox[["xmin"]], lat1 = bbox[["ymin"]], lng2 = bbox[["xmax"]], lat2 = bbox[["ymax"]] ) }) # Map clicks: choose boroughs to test, or toggle a local restriction observeEvent(input$map_shape_click, { req(ready()) click <- input$map_shape_click req(click$id) idx <- match(click$id, pop_tbl$borough_name) req(!is.na(idx)) if (identical(input$click_mode, "restrict")) { current <- restricted() if (idx %in% current) { restricted(setdiff(current, idx)) return() } trial <- c(current, idx) share <- teaching_params()$local_restrictions$max_pop_share if (length(current) > 0 && sum(pop_tbl$pop[trial]) / sum(pop_tbl$pop) > share) { shiny::showNotification( sprintf("At most %d%% of people can be under local restrictions at once: lift one first.", round(100 * share)), type = "error" ) return() } if (budget_info()$budget - other_cost(trial) < -1e-6) { shiny::showNotification("Not enough money left this report to restrict another area.", type = "error") return() } restricted(trial) return() } # choose mode: toggle the borough, and test only chosen boroughs current <- chosen() chosen(if (idx %in% current) setdiff(current, idx) else sort(c(current, idx))) if (!identical(input$where, "chosen")) { shiny::updateRadioButtons(session, "where", selected = "chosen") } }) # measure labels show this place's prices (they scale with population) observe({ req(ready()) budget <- budget_info() shiny::updateCheckboxInput(session, "tracing", label = sprintf("Contact tracing · %s", format_round(budget$tracing_cost))) testing <- budget$testing shiny::updateCheckboxInput( session, "build_testing", label = if (isTRUE(testing$can_build)) { sprintf("Improve PCR · %s once, takes %d reports (cheaper, more tests)", format_round(testing$build_cost), testing$build_turns) } else if (isTRUE(testing$building)) "Improve PCR · under way" else "Improve PCR · labs at their best" ) shiny::updateCheckboxInput( session, "develop_rapid", label = if (isTRUE(testing$can_develop_rapid)) { sprintf("Develop rapid tests · %s a report for %d reports (cheap home tests; lockdown works better)", format_round(testing$rapid_cost), testing$rapid_turns) } else if (isTRUE(testing$developing_rapid)) { sprintf("Develop rapid tests · under way, %s a report", format_round(testing$rapid_cost)) } else "Develop rapid tests · done" ) }) # London-wide measures with this place's prices; lockdown only once there # have been enough deaths or hospitals are filling up output$interventions_ui <- shiny::renderUI({ req(ready()) budget <- budget_info() defs <- budget$interventions allowed <- !identical(budget$lockdown_allowed, FALSE) trigger <- teaching_params()$lockdown_trigger names <- sprintf("%s · %s", defs$label, format_round(defs$cost)) if (!allowed) { names[defs$id == "distancing"] <- sprintf( "%s · only after %d deaths or beds %d%% full", defs$label[defs$id == "distancing"], trigger$deaths, round(100 * trigger$bed_share) ) } selected <- shiny::isolate(input$interventions) %||% character() if (!allowed) selected <- setdiff(selected, "distancing") boxes <- shiny::checkboxGroupInput( session$ns("interventions"), label = NULL, choiceNames = as.list(names), choiceValues = as.list(defs$id), selected = selected ) if (!allowed) { boxes <- htmltools::tagQuery(boxes)$ find("input")$filter(function(x, i) identical(x$attribs$value, "distancing"))$ addAttrs(disabled = NA)$ parent()$addAttrs(style = "opacity: 0.5;")$ allTags() } boxes }) # what each control measure will do next turn (lag, fading, capacity) output$measure_status <- shiny::renderUI({ req(ready()) budget <- budget_info() lines <- character() for (id in selected_interventions()) { def <- intervention_defs[intervention_defs$id == id, ] next_streak <- get_streak(budget$streaks, id) + 1L strength <- intervention_strength(next_streak, def$lag, def$fatigue) lines <- c(lines, if (strength == 0) { sprintf("%s starts working the report after next.", def$label) } else { sprintf("%s: %d%% strength.", def$label, round(100 * strength)) }) } if (length(restricted()) > 0) { lr <- teaching_params()$local_restrictions next_streaks <- budget$local_streaks[restricted()] + 1L strengths <- vapply(next_streaks, intervention_strength, numeric(1), lag = lr$lag, fatigue = lr$fatigue) lines <- c(lines, sprintf( "Restrictions on %d area%s: %s.", length(restricted()), if (length(restricted()) == 1) "" else "s", if (all(strengths == 0)) "start working the report after next" else paste0(round(100 * max(strengths)), "% strength") )) } if (isTRUE(input$tracing)) { lines <- c(lines, sprintf("Tracing: up to %d cases a report.", teaching_params()$tracing$capacity)) } if (isTRUE(budget$testing$developing_rapid)) { lines <- c(lines, sprintf("Rapid tests: %d report%s to go.", budget$testing$rapid_left, if (budget$testing$rapid_left == 1) "" else "s")) } if (isTRUE(budget$testing$building)) { lines <- c(lines, sprintf("Building testing: %d report%s left, half capacity meanwhile.", budget$testing$build_left, if (budget$testing$build_left == 1) "" else "s")) } if (length(lines) == 0) { return(NULL) } shiny::HTML(paste(lines, collapse = "
")) }) # test choices show today's price and wait; antigen is always listed but # greyed out until testing has been built up to a level that has it output$test_type_ui <- shiny::renderUI({ req(ready()) budget <- budget_info() testing <- budget$testing ag_available <- isTRUE(testing$ag_available) wait_days <- testing$delays$pcr * teaching_params()$report_days pcr_label <- sprintf("PCR · %s each · %s", budget$costs[["pcr"]], if (wait_days == 0) "instant" else paste(wait_days, "days")) ag_label <- if (ag_available) { sprintf("Antigen · %s each · instant", budget$costs[["ag"]]) } else { "Antigen · develop rapid tests first" } selected <- if (ag_available) shiny::isolate(input$test_type) %||% "pcr" else "pcr" buttons <- shiny::radioButtons( session$ns("test_type"), label = "Which test", choiceNames = list(ag_label, pcr_label), choiceValues = list("ag", "pcr"), selected = selected ) if (!ag_available) { buttons <- htmltools::tagQuery(buttons)$ find("input")$filter(function(x, i) identical(x$attribs$value, "ag"))$ addAttrs(disabled = NA)$ parent()$addAttrs(style = "opacity: 0.5;")$ allTags() } buttons }) # one line saying what this plan will do output$allocation_summary <- shiny::renderText({ req(ready()) p <- plan() budget <- budget_info() n_tests <- sum(p$allocations$n_ag + p$allocations$n_pcr) test_name <- if (p$test == "ag") "antigen" else "PCR" if (p$asked <= 0) { return("No tests planned.") } if (length(p$targets) == 0) { return(if (p$where == "positives") "No positives yet, so no tests." else "Pick areas on the map.") } where_txt <- if (p$where == "everywhere") paste("all", nrow(pop_tbl), "areas") else paste(length(p$targets), if (length(p$targets) == 1) "area" else "areas") txt <- paste0(format(n_tests, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), " ", test_name, " tests in ", where_txt, ".") # symptomatic testing can only reach the people who come forward if (identical(input$who, "symptomatic") && !is.null(budget$pool_size)) { reachable <- sum(pmin(p$allocations$n_ag + p$allocations$n_pcr, budget$pool_size)) if (reachable < n_tests) { txt <- paste0(txt, " Only about ", format(reachable, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), " people come forward.") } } if (p$cut_down) { txt <- paste0(txt, " Cut to fit the money left.") } txt }) observe({ if (!ready()) { return() } latest <- observed_this_turn() total_tests <- sum(latest$n, na.rm = TRUE) positives <- sum(latest$positives, na.rm = TRUE) output$turn_positivity <- shiny::renderText({ if (total_tests == 0) { "" } else { paste0("Last turn: ", round(100 * positives / total_tests, 1), "% positive") } }) }) # Update map with results, planned tests, chosen and restricted boroughs observe({ if (!ready()) { shiny::invalidateLater(100, session) return() } if (!map_ready()) { shiny::invalidateLater(100, session) return() } res <- observed_this_turn() allocs <- plan()$allocations layers <- map_layers(res, reports(), pop_tbl, boros$borough_name) layer <- layers[[input$map_layer %||% "positivity"]] # fixed steps, pale blue to deep red: the map only ever gets deeper as # things get worse, never rescaled. Nothing reported: dark slate. fill_cols <- map_colours(layer$values, layer$breaks) # hover: every layer's number for the area, plus the plan labels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(boros)), function(i) { name <- boros$borough_name[i] pos <- layers$positivity$values[i] result_txt <- if (is.na(pos)) "No test results this report" else sprintf("%.1f%% of %s tests positive", 100 * pos, format(layers$positivity$tests[i], big.mark = ",")) hosp_txt <- sprintf("%s admissions, %s deaths reported", layers$admissions$counts[i], layers$deaths$counts[i]) planned <- allocs$n_ag[i] + allocs$n_pcr[i] alloc_txt <- if (planned > 0) sprintf("
Planned: %d tests", planned) else "" restrict_txt <- if (i %in% restricted()) "
Restricted" else "" htmltools::HTML(paste0("", name, "
", result_txt, "
", hosp_txt, alloc_txt, restrict_txt)) }) # outlines: red = restricted, blue = chosen for testing is_restricted <- seq_len(nrow(boros)) %in% restricted() is_chosen <- seq_len(nrow(boros)) %in% chosen() & identical(input$where, "chosen") outline_col <- ifelse(is_restricted, "#ff4d4d", ifelse(is_chosen, "#4fc3f7", "#ffffff")) outline_weight <- ifelse(is_restricted | is_chosen, 3.5, 0.8) # the first patient's area is lit: violet (outside the positivity # scale) until results come back from there, and a violet outline all # game unless one of the player's own outlines takes priority first <- first_report() if (!is.null(first) && !is.na(first$index)) { f <- first$index if (identical(input$map_layer %||% "positivity", "positivity") && is.na(layer$values[f])) { fill_cols[f] <- "#b56cf0" } if (!is_restricted[f] && !is_chosen[f]) { outline_col[f] <- "#e0b3ff" outline_weight[f] <- 3 } } proxy <- leaflet::leafletProxy(ns("map"), data = boros) |> leaflet::removeControl("positivity_legend") |> leaflet::addLegend( layerId = "positivity_legend", position = "bottomright", colors = c("#3d4f61", map_palette), labels = c(layer$none_label, layer$step_labels), title = layer$title, opacity = 0.9 ) |> leaflet::clearGroup("boroughs") |> leaflet::clearGroup("alloc_markers") |> leaflet::addPolygons( layerId = boros$borough_name, weight = outline_weight, color = outline_col, opacity = 0.9, fillOpacity = 0.9, fillColor = fill_cols, label = labels, group = "boroughs", highlight = leaflet::highlightOptions(weight = 2, bringToFront = TRUE) ) # (no circles for planned tests: they covered the map; # Observation model -----------------------------------------------------------

#' Create an empty observation state
#'
#' @return A list storing a delay queue and observation history.
#' @export
init_observation_state <- function() {
  # plain data frames (not tibbles): these are built every turn, and base R
  # tables are much quicker when bots play thousands of games
  empty <- data.frame(
    borough_index = integer(),
    borough_name = character(),
    type = character(),
    n = integer(),
    positives = integer(),
    true_pos = integer(),
    infectious_pos = integer(),
    mode = character(),
    source = character(),
    turn_sampled = integer(),
    turn_available = integer(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  list(queue = empty, history = empty)
}

#' Simulate testing outcomes with delays
#'
#' @param state Observation state list.
#' @param turn Current turn (integer).
#' @param allocations Tidy tibble with columns borough_index, borough_name,
#'   n_pcr, n_ag.
#' @param truth_incidence Numeric vector of underlying infections per borough.
#' @param pop_tbl Population tibble with `pop` column.
#' @param params List with components `sens`, `spec`, `delays`, `prev_floor`,
#'   and optionally `sampling_mode`, `sampling_pool_frac` and `care_seeking`
#'   (per-borough multiplier, symptomatic mode only), and `detectable`
#'   (list with `ag` / `pcr`: per-borough people still test-positive from
#'   recent infections, random mode only).
#' @return Updated state with queue/history and tibble of available results.
#' @export
observe_tests <- function(
    state,
    turn,
    allocations,
    truth_incidence,
    pop_tbl,
    params) {
  if (missing(state) || is.null(state$queue)) {
    stop("state must be created with init_observation_state()")
  }

  if (!all(c("borough_index", "borough_name", "n_pcr", "n_ag") %in% names(allocations))) {
    stop("allocations missing required columns")
  }

  if (length(truth_incidence) != nrow(allocations)) {
    stop("truth_incidence must align with allocations")
  }

  prev_floor <- params$prev_floor %||% 1e-6

  prev <- truth_incidence / pop_tbl$pop

  sampling_mode <- params$sampling_mode %||% "random"
  if (sampling_mode == "symptomatic") {
    pool_frac <- params$sampling_pool_frac %||% 0.1
    pool_frac <- max(min(pool_frac, 1), 1e-6)

    # some boroughs are less likely to come forward for a test, so fewer of
    # their infected people end up in the tested pool (1 = no bias)
    care_seeking <- params$care_seeking %||% 1
    # people with no symptoms never come forward
    symptomatic_share <- params$symptomatic_share %||% 1
    prev <- truth_incidence * symptomatic_share * care_seeking / (pop_tbl$pop * pool_frac)
  }
  prev <- pmax(prev, prev_floor)
  prev <- pmin(prev, 0.9)

  se <- params$sens
  sp <- params$spec
  delays <- params$delays

  simulate_type <- function(type, n_col) {
    n_tests <- allocations[[n_col]]
    if (all(n_tests == 0)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    sens <- se[[type]]
    spec <- sp[[type]]
    delay <- delays[[type]]

    # random testing finds anyone still test-positive from recent turns,
    # but only this turn's infections are still spreading
    prev_type <- prev
    current_share <- rep(1, length(n_tests))
    detectable <- params$detectable[[type]]
    if (sampling_mode == "random" && !is.null(detectable)) {
      prev_type <- pmin(pmax(detectable / pop_tbl$pop, prev_floor), 0.9)
      current_share <- ifelse(detectable > 0, pmin(1, truth_incidence / detectable), 0)
    }

    p_star <- sens * prev_type + (1 - spec) * (1 - prev_type)
    p_star <- pmin(pmax(p_star, 0), 1)

    positives <- stats::rbinom(length(n_tests), size = n_tests, prob = p_star)

    # how many of those positives are real infections, and how many of
    # those are still infectious (both hidden from players)
    true_share <- ifelse(p_star > 0, pmin(1, sens * prev_type / p_star), 0)
    true_pos <- stats::rbinom(length(positives), size = positives, prob = true_share)
    infectious_pos <- stats::rbinom(length(true_pos), size = true_pos, prob = current_share)

    results <- data.frame(
      borough_index = allocations$borough_index,
      borough_name = allocations$borough_name,
      type = type,
      n = as.integer(n_tests),
      positives = as.integer(positives),
      true_pos = as.integer(true_pos),
      infectious_pos = as.integer(infectious_pos),
      mode = sampling_mode,
      source = params$source %||% "player",
      turn_sampled = as.integer(turn),
      turn_available = as.integer(turn + delay),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    results[results$n > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  ag_results <- simulate_type("ag", "n_ag")
  pcr_results <- simulate_type("pcr", "n_pcr")

  # rbind of NULLs is NULL; start from the empty table so columns always exist
  new_results <- rbind(state$queue[0, , drop = FALSE], ag_results, pcr_results)

  # results due now come back; later ones wait in the queue
  prior_queue <- state$queue
  due <- prior_queue$turn_available <= turn
  ready <- new_results$turn_available <= turn
  available_now <- rbind(prior_queue[due, , drop = FALSE], new_results[ready, , drop = FALSE])
  retained_queue <- rbind(prior_queue[!due, , drop = FALSE], new_results[!ready, , drop = FALSE])

  available_now <- available_now[order(available_now$borough_index, available_now$type), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(available_now) <- NULL
  rownames(retained_queue) <- NULL
  history <- rbind(state$history, available_now)
  rownames(history) <- NULL

  list(
    queue = retained_queue,
    history = history,
    available = available_now,
    new_results = new_results
  )
}

#' Summarise testing spend against budget
#'
#' @param allocations Tibble with columns n_pcr, n_ag.
#' @param costs Named numeric vector or list with entries pcr, ag.
#' @param budget Total budget available this turn.
#' @return A list with total spend and remaining budget.
#' @export
summarise_budget <- function(allocations, costs, budget) {
  cost_pcr <- costs[["pcr"]] %||% 0
  cost_ag <- costs[["ag"]] %||% 0
  spend <- sum(allocations$n_pcr * cost_pcr + allocations$n_ag * cost_ag)

  list(
    spend = spend,
    remaining = budget - spend,
    within_budget = spend <= budget + 1e-6
  )
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.null(x)) y else x
}
