# Place library: choose a country or city, play at the next admin level down --
#
# prepare_place_library.R (run once, offline) turns global admin boundaries
# and a population raster into one small .rds per place plus an index.
# At run time the app only looks things up here: no internet needed.
#
#   country -> the coarsest admin level (1, 2, 3) giving 10-600 areas
#   city    -> the coarsest admin level (2, 3) giving at least 10 areas inside
#              the urban radius; otherwise the 10 nearest at the finest level
#   Places that cannot reach 10 areas are left out (thin games are not playable).
#
# Each place file holds:
#   meta     one-row data frame (id, label, type, country, level, ...)
#   inputs   bundle shaped like load_inputs() (boros, nb, A, K, pop_tbl, ...)
#   context  sf of surrounding units (not in play) for the backdrop map


# ---- choosing units (used when building the library) ------------------------

#' Pick the admin units that make up a city
#'
#' Blunt rule: units whose centroid is within `radius_km` of the city point,
#' plus the unit containing the point. Too few (< `n_min`) -> widen to the
#' `n_min` nearest units, and flag it. Too many -> keep the `n_max` nearest.
#'
#' @param units_sf Candidate units (WGS84), e.g. all admin-2 in the country.
#' @param city_lon,city_lat City point.
#' @param radius_km Urban radius, e.g. sqrt(urban_area_km2 / pi).
#' @return Row indices of `units_sf` in play, nearest first, with attribute
#'   `widened` = TRUE when the radius gave fewer than `n_min` units.
#' @export
pick_city_units <- function(units_sf, city_lon, city_lat, radius_km,
                            n_min = 10, n_max = 60) {

  city_point <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(city_lon, city_lat)), crs = 4326)

  # Distance from the city point to each unit centroid (km)
  centroids <- centroid_lonlat(units_sf)
  dist_km <- haversine_km(centroids[, 1], centroids[, 2], city_lon, city_lat)

  # Unit that contains the city point (always in play)
  contains_city <- suppressMessages(lengths(sf::st_intersects(units_sf, city_point)) > 0)

  in_play <- which(dist_km <= radius_km | contains_city)
  widened <- length(in_play) < n_min

  # Too few units: widen to the nearest n_min
  if (widened) {
    in_play <- order(dist_km)[seq_len(min(n_min, length(dist_km)))]
  }

  # Too many units: keep the nearest
  in_play <- in_play[order(dist_km[in_play])]
  if (length(in_play) > n_max) {
    in_play <- in_play[seq_len(n_max)]
  }

  attr(in_play, "widened") <- widened
  in_play
}


#' Drop far-off islands from a country
#'
#' Units are linked if they touch or their centroids are within `max_gap_km`.
#' Only the most populous linked cluster is kept, so the Azores, Hawaii or
#' Puerto Rico (with its own nearby islands) drop out of a mainland game.
#'
#' @param units_sf Units (WGS84) with a `pop` column.
#' @return Logical vector, TRUE = keep.
#' @export
keep_mainland <- function(units_sf, max_gap_km = 500) {
  n_units <- nrow(units_sf)
  if (n_units < 3) {
    return(rep(TRUE, n_units))
  }

  # Links: touching polygons ...
  touches <- suppressMessages(sf::st_touches(units_sf, sparse = FALSE))

  # ... or centroids close together
  centroids <- centroid_lonlat(units_sf)
  dist_km <- outer(seq_len(n_units), seq_len(n_units), function(i, j) {
    haversine_km(centroids[i, 1], centroids[i, 2], centroids[j, 1], centroids[j, 2])
  })
  linked <- touches | dist_km <= max_gap_km

  # Label clusters by spreading a label along links until nothing changes
  cluster <- seq_len(n_units)
  repeat {
    new_cluster <- apply(linked, 1, function(row) min(cluster[row]))
    new_cluster <- pmin(cluster, new_cluster)
    if (identical(new_cluster, cluster)) break
    cluster <- new_cluster
  }

  # Keep the cluster with the most people
  cluster_pop <- tapply(units_sf$pop, cluster, sum)
  main_cluster <- as.integer(names(cluster_pop)[which.max(cluster_pop)])
  cluster == main_cluster
}


#' Simplify polygons for display only
#'
#' Tolerance scales with the size of the place (bbox diagonal / 500), so a
#' country and a city both keep about the same visual detail.
#' Adjacency and population are always computed on the full geometry first.
#' @export
simplify_for_display <- function(units_sf) {
  bbox <- sf::st_bbox(units_sf)
  diagonal_deg <- sqrt((bbox[["xmax"]] - bbox[["xmin"]])^2 + (bbox[["ymax"]] - bbox[["ymin"]])^2)
  tolerance_deg <- diagonal_deg / 500

  old_s2 <- sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
  on.exit(suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(old_s2)))

  simple <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_simplify(units_sf, preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = tolerance_deg))
  simple <- sf::st_make_valid(simple)
  simple
}


# ---- looking places up (used by the app) ------------------------------------

#' Read the place index
#' @param library_dir Folder written by prepare_place_library.R.
#' @export
read_place_index <- function(library_dir = file.path("locations", "library")) {
  index_path <- file.path(library_dir, "index.rds")
  if (!file.exists(index_path)) {
    stop("No place library at ", library_dir, "; run prepare_place_library.R first")
  }
  readRDS(index_path)
}

#' Find places matching free text
#'
#' Case- and accent-insensitive. Exact name matches first (countries before
#' cities, bigger cities first), then names that start with the text, then
#' names that contain it.
#'
#' @param query Text typed by the user, e.g. "lisbon" or "Kenya".
#' @param index Place index from read_place_index().
#' @param n Maximum number of matches.
#' @return Rows of `index`, best first.
#' @export
find_place <- function(query, index, n = 10) {
  query_key <- name_key(query)
  if (!nzchar(query_key)) {
    return(index[0, ])
  }

  # One row per (place, searchable name)
  name_lists <- strsplit(index$search_names, "|", fixed = TRUE)
  long <- data.frame(
    row = rep(seq_len(nrow(index)), lengths(name_lists)),
    key = name_key(unlist(name_lists))
  )

  # Score: 1 exact, 2 starts with, 3 contains
  long$score <- ifelse(long$key == query_key, 1,
                ifelse(startsWith(long$key, query_key), 2,
                ifelse(grepl(query_key, long$key, fixed = TRUE), 3, NA)))
  long <- long[!is.na(long$score), ]
  if (nrow(long) == 0) {
    return(index[0, ])
  }

  # Best score per place
  best <- stats::aggregate(score ~ row, data = long, FUN = min)
  hits <- index[best$row, ]
  hits$score <- best$score

  # Countries before cities, then bigger places first
  type_rank <- ifelse(hits$type == "country", 1, 2)
  hits <- hits[order(hits$score, type_rank, -hits$pop_total), ]
  hits$score <- NULL
  utils::head(hits, n)
}

#' Load one place: its game inputs and backdrop
#'
#' @param place_id `id` from the index.
#' @param gravity list(alpha, beta) for the kernel, rebuilt on load.
#' @return list(meta, inputs, context). For the built-in London entry the
#'   inputs come from data/ via load_inputs() (unchanged default).
#' @export
load_place <- function(place_id, index, library_dir = file.path("locations", "library"),
                       data_dir = "data", gravity = list(alpha = 1, beta = 2)) {
  row <- index[index$id == place_id, ]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) {
    stop("Unknown place id: ", place_id)
  }

  place <- readRDS(file.path(library_dir, row$file))

  # London keeps the original 33-borough inputs the game was built on
  if (isTRUE(row$use_builtin)) {
    place$inputs <- load_inputs(data_dir = data_dir)
  }

  # K is not stored in the library; rebuild it from centroids, areas, population
  if (is.null(place$inputs$K)) {
    boros <- place$inputs$boros
    place$inputs$K <- gravity_kernel_from_points(
      boros$centroid_lon, boros$centroid_lat, boros$area_km2,
      place$inputs$pop_tbl$pop, place$inputs$pop_tbl$borough_name,
      alpha = gravity$alpha, beta = gravity$beta
    )
  }

  # Planar copy is not stored in the library; re-derive it
  if (is.null(place$inputs$boros_planar)) {
    planar_crs <- local_equal_area_crs(place$inputs$boros)
    place$inputs$boros_planar <- sf::st_transform(place$inputs$boros, planar_crs)
  }

  place
}

# Lower case, strip accents and punctuation: "Sao Paulo" with accents -> "sao paulo".
# Base R only (no stringi), so it also runs in the browser (Shinylive).
accented_letters <- "\u00C0\u00C1\u00C2\u00C3\u00C4\u00C5\u00E0\u00E1\u00E2\u00E3\u00E4\u00E5\u0100\u0101\u0102\u0103\u0104\u0105\u00C7\u00E7\u0106\u0107\u010C\u010D\u010E\u010F\u0110\u0111\u00C8\u00C9\u00CA\u00CB\u00E8\u00E9\u00EA\u00EB\u0112\u0113\u0116\u0117\u0118\u0119\u011A\u011B\u011E\u011F\u0122\u0123\u00CC\u00CD\u00CE\u00CF\u00EC\u00ED\u00EE\u00EF\u012A\u012B\u012E\u012F\u0130\u0131\u0136\u0137\u0139\u013A\u013B\u013C\u013D\u013E\u0141\u0142\u00D1\u00F1\u0143\u0144\u0145\u0146\u0147\u0148\u00D2\u00D3\u00D4\u00D5\u00D6\u00D8\u00F2\u00F3\u00F4\u00F5\u00F6\u00F8\u014C\u014D\u0150\u0151\u0154\u0155\u0158\u0159\u015A\u015B\u015E\u015F\u0160\u0161\u0218\u0219\u0162\u0163\u0164\u0165\u021A\u021B\u00D9\u00DA\u00DB\u00DC\u00F9\u00FA\u00FB\u00FC\u016A\u016B\u016E\u016F\u0170\u0171\u0172\u0173\u00DD\u00FD\u00FF\u0178\u0179\u017A\u017B\u017C\u017D\u017E"
plain_letters    <- "AAAAAAaaaaaaAaAaAaCcCcCcDdDdEEEEeeeeEeEeEeEeGgGgIIIIiiiiIiIiIiKkLlLlLlLlNnNnNnNnOOOOOOooooooOoOoRrRrSsSsSsSsTtTtTtUUUUuuuuUuUuUuUuYyyYZzZzZz"

name_key <- function(x) {
  x <- enc2utf8(as.character(x))
  x <- chartr(accented_letters, plain_letters, x)
  x <- gsub("\u00DF", "ss", x)                # German sharp s
  x <- gsub("[\u00C6\u00E6]", "ae", x)   # ligature ae
  x <- gsub("[\u0152\u0153]", "oe", x)   # ligature oe
  x <- tolower(x)
  x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", " ", x)
  trimws(x)
}

# Centroids as a lon/lat matrix (planar centroid of lon/lat polygons;
# fine for picking nearby units, no s2 needed)
centroid_lonlat <- function(units_sf) {
  old_s2 <- suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE))
  on.exit(suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(old_s2)))
  centroids <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(units_sf)))
  sf::st_coordinates(centroids)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]
}


# ---- kernel and distance helpers (shared with build_location_inputs.R) ------

#' Gravity kernel from unit centroids and areas
#'
#' Same kernel as gravity_kernel(), from stored numbers instead of polygons
#' (the place library keeps these, so K is rebuilt on load and alpha/beta
#' can be changed at game time).
#'
#' @param lon,lat Unit centroids (degrees).
#' @param area_km2 Unit areas (km^2), for the within-unit distance.
#' @param pop Unit populations.
#' @param unit_names Names for the dimnames.
#' @export
gravity_kernel_from_points <- function(lon, lat, area_km2, pop, unit_names,
                                       alpha = 1, beta = 2) {
  n_units <- length(pop)

  # Centroid-to-centroid great-circle distances in km
  dist_km <- outer(seq_len(n_units), seq_len(n_units), function(i, j) {
    haversine_km(lon[i], lat[i], lon[j], lat[j])
  })

  # Within-unit distance for the diagonal (km)
  self_km <- (2 / 3) * sqrt(area_km2 / pi)
  diag(dist_km) <- self_km

  if (any(dist_km <= 0)) {
    stop("Zero distance between units; check for duplicate or empty polygons")
  }

  # Gravity weights: row = source unit, column = destination unit,
  # so each column carries the destination population
  pop_weight <- matrix(pop^alpha, nrow = n_units, ncol = n_units, byrow = TRUE)
  W <- pop_weight / dist_km^beta

  # Row-normalise so each row sums to 1
  K <- W / rowSums(W)

  dimnames(K) <- list(unit_names, unit_names)
  K
}

# Great-circle distance in km
haversine_km <- function(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) {
  to_rad <- pi / 180
  d_lat <- (lat2 - lat1) * to_rad
  d_lon <- (lon2 - lon1) * to_rad
  a <- sin(d_lat / 2)^2 + cos(lat1 * to_rad) * cos(lat2 * to_rad) * sin(d_lon / 2)^2
  6371 * 2 * asin(pmin(1, sqrt(a)))
}

# Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on the units (metres).
# Works anywhere in the world without having to pick a UTM zone.
local_equal_area_crs <- function(units_wgs84) {
  bbox <- sf::st_bbox(units_wgs84)
  lon_0 <- mean(c(bbox[["xmin"]], bbox[["xmax"]]))
  lat_0 <- mean(c(bbox[["ymin"]], bbox[["ymax"]]))
  sprintf("+proj=laea +lat_0=%.4f +lon_0=%.4f +units=m +datum=WGS84", lat_0, lon_0)
}


# ---- data licences ----------------------------------------------------------

#' Attach the boundary licence to each place and drop restricted ones
#'
#' geoBoundaries data comes under each country's own licence (mostly ODbL,
#' CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain). Places whose boundaries need direct
#' permission from the provider are removed, so the library can be shared.
#'
#' @param index Place index.
#' @param meta_csv geoBoundariesOpen-meta.csv (boundaryISO, boundaryType, boundaryLicense).
#' @return Index with `boundary_license` and `license_source`, restricted places dropped.
#' @export
add_boundary_licenses <- function(index, meta_csv) {
  gb_meta <- utils::read.csv(meta_csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  gb_meta <- gb_meta[!duplicated(gb_meta[, c("boundaryISO", "boundaryType")]), ]

  key_index <- paste(index$iso3, index$level)
  key_meta <- paste(gb_meta$boundaryISO, gb_meta$boundaryType)
  hit <- match(key_index, key_meta)

  index$boundary_license <- gb_meta$boundaryLicense[hit]
  index$license_source <- gb_meta$licenseSource[hit]
  index$boundary_license[is.na(hit)] <- "Unknown: check geoBoundaries metadata"

  # Not freely redistributable
  restricted <- grepl("Direct Permission", index$boundary_license)
  if (any(restricted)) {
    message("Dropping places with restricted boundary licences: ",
            paste(index$label[restricted], collapse = ", "))
  }
  index[!restricted, ]
}

# Scenario presets ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# One row per disease. Each one is meant to reward a different strategy, so
# that no single approach always works:
#   measles (current vaccination)  only just spreading: watch, act locally
#   measles (low vaccination)      explosive: near impossible to contain
#   COVID-like                     silent spread: cannot be contained, only slowed
#   Ebola-like                     severe, slow, often dies out: hospital reports
#   Nipah-like                     a cluster that fizzles: act on hospital cases, hold back
#   SARS-like                      spreads only once sick: find and isolate the sick
#   Mpox-like                      slow, close contact: contact tracing
#   MERS-like                      hospital clusters: hospital reports, act locally
#   Pandemic flu                   fast, deadly wave: flatten it, protect hospitals
#   Smallpox-like                  rash before spread: ring response (trace, isolate)
#   Polio-like                     99% silent: only random sampling sees it
#
# Columns:
#   Rt               R per generation if nobody were immune (R0); effective R at
#                    the start is Rt x susceptible_frac
#   k                superspreading (small = a few people cause most spread)
#   imports_prob     chance of an introduction from outside per area per
#   lambda_import    report, and its mean size. All 0: the game is one
#                    outbreak from one infected person (introductions would
#                    restart outbreaks that had died out and add clusters
#                    unrelated to it)
#   susceptible_frac share who can catch it at the start (vaccination, past infection)
#   death_ifr        share of infected people who die
#   death_delay_days days from infection to death
#   test_level       PCR at the start: 1 reference lab, 2 hospital labs
#                    (rapid antigen tests have to be developed)
#   asymptomatic     share of infections with no symptoms (never come forward)
#   presymptomatic   share of a case's spread before symptoms (a case found
#                    through its symptoms has already done this much damage)
#   delay_decay      isolation value left after each generation of result delay
#   hosp_frac        share of infections admitted to hospital (always reported)
#   gen_days         days per generation of infection
#   hosp_delay_days  days from infection to hospital admission
#   kernel_key       spatial kernel ("measles" = less mobility)

scenario_catalog <- function() {
  diseases <- tibble::tribble(
    ~id,               ~Rt,  ~k,   ~imports_prob, ~lambda_import, ~susceptible_frac, ~death_ifr, ~death_delay_days, ~test_level, ~asymptomatic, ~presymptomatic, ~delay_decay, ~hosp_frac, ~gen_days, ~hosp_delay_days, ~kernel_key,
    "custom",          1.3,  0.5,  0,             0.5,            1,                 0.002,      20,                2L,          0.2,           0.3,             0.5,          0.02,       5L,        10,               "default",
    "measles_current", 15,   1.5,  0,             0.2,            0.08,              0.001,      24,                2L,          0.05,          0.3,             0.6,          0.1,        12L,       12,               "measles",
    "measles_low_vax", 15,   1.5,  0,             0.2,            0.2,               0.001,      24,                2L,          0.05,          0.3,             0.6,          0.1,        12L,       12,               "measles",
    "covid_early",     2.0,  0.25, 0,             1.0,            0.9,               0.002,      20,                2L,          0.45,          0.45,            0.4,          0.03,       5L,        10,               "default",
    "ebola_like",      1.5,  0.4,  0,             0.2,            1.0,               0.5,        15,                1L,          0.05,          0,               0.85,         0.5,        15L,       15,               "default",
    "nipah_like",      0.8,  0.1,  0,             0.2,            1.0,               0.6,        20,                1L,          0.1,           0.1,             0.8,          0.6,        10L,       10,               "default",
    "sars_like",       2.5,  0.16, 0,             0.3,            1.0,               0.1,        24,                1L,          0.1,           0.05,            0.8,          0.6,        8L,        8,                "default",
    "mpox_like",       1.6,  0.3,  0,             0.5,            0.8,               0.001,      25,                2L,          0.1,           0.2,             0.8,          0.05,       10L,       14,               "default",
    "mers_like",       1.3,  0.1,  0,             0.2,            1.0,               0.35,       15,                1L,          0.2,           0.05,            0.8,          0.7,        7L,        7,                "default",
    "flu_pandemic",    2.0,  1.0,  0,             1.0,            1.0,               0.02,       14,                2L,          0.3,           0.3,             0.35,         0.05,       3L,        7,                "default",
    "smallpox_like",   4.0,  0.6,  0,             0.2,            0.5,               0.3,        21,                1L,          0,             0,               0.9,          0.5,        15L,       14,               "default",
    "polio_like",      6.0,  1.0,  0,             0.5,            0.25,              0.0005,     30,                2L,          0.99,          0.5,             0.7,          0.005,      12L,       14,               "default"
  )

  # names and what each one was (the blurb is shown at the start of the review)
  text <- tibble::tribble(
    ~id, ~label, ~objective, ~blurb,
    "custom", "Custom (no preset)", "Use default parameters or adjust manually.",
    "A new respiratory infection with moderate spread.",
    "measles_current", "Measles-like (current vaccination)", "High transmissibility with current vaccination levels and reduced mobility.",
    paste(
      "A measles-like virus: extremely contagious through the air (each case would infect about 15 people",
      "if nobody were immune). Almost everyone infected becomes ill, and cases spread it for a few days",

    ),
    "measles_low_vax", "Measles-like (low vaccination)", "High transmissibility with low vaccination coverage and reduced mobility.",
    paste(
      "A measles-like virus: extremely contagious through the air (each case would infect about 15 people",

    ),
    "covid_early", "COVID-like (early, superspreading)", "Superspreading with higher imports and fast early growth.",
    paste(

    ),
    "ebola_like", "Ebola-like (sustained, high mortality)", "Sustained transmission with high mortality and moderate clustering.",
    paste(
      "An Ebola-like virus: spread through close contact with very sick people, with almost no spread",

    ),
    "nipah_like", "Nipah-like (spillover cluster)", "Low average spread with strong clustering, from one jump from animals.",
    paste(
      "A Nipah-like virus: it jumped from an animal into one person, and spreads little between",
      "people (each case infects fewer than one other on average) but kills most of those it",
      "infects. Clusters like this usually die out on their own."
    ),
    "sars_like", "SARS-like (spreads once sick)", "Fast spread with superspreading, but almost none before symptoms.",
    paste(
      "A SARS-like coronavirus: each case would infect two or three others, a few infect many, and",
      "most need hospital care. Almost all spread happens after symptoms start, so finding and",

    ),
    "mpox_like", "Mpox-like (slow, close contact)", "Slow spread through close contact, with clear symptoms.",
    paste(
      "An mpox-like virus: spread by close contact, slowly (a new generation every 10 days or so),",

    paste(
      "A MERS-like coronavirus: most cases are severe and end up in hospital, a third of them die,",

    ),
    "flu_pandemic", "Pandemic flu (1918-like)", "Fast, deadly influenza that nobody is immune to.",
    paste(
      "A new pandemic influenza, like 1918: nobody is immune, a new generation of infections every",

    ),

    paste(
      "A smallpox-like virus: each case would infect about four others, but only after the rash",
      "appears, and a generation takes about two weeks. Older people are protected by past",

      "the contacts of every case (a ring response) is how smallpox was eradicated."
    ),
    "polio_like", "Polio-like (silent spread)", "Almost every infection is silent; very few cases are ever seen.",
    paste(
      "A polio-like virus: highly contagious, but 99 in 100 infections cause no symptoms and only",

      "hospital reports misses almost all of it; only testing a random sample of people finds it.",
      "A quarter of people here are unvaccinated."
    )
  )

  diseases |>
    dplyr::left_join(text, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      # kept for older code paths: the outbreak now starts from one person
      seed_borough = NA_integer_,
      seed_cases = 1L
    )
}

scenario_lookup <- function(id, catalog = scenario_catalog()) {
  if (is.null(id) || length(id) == 0 || is.na(id)) {
    id <- "custom"
  }
  match_idx <- match(id, catalog$id)
  if (is.na(match_idx)) {
    match_idx <- match("custom", catalog$id)
  }
  catalog[match_idx, , drop = FALSE]
}

scenario_choices <- function(catalog = scenario_catalog()) {
  stats::setNames(catalog$id, catalog$label)
}

# Scoring helpers ------------------------------------------------------------

#' Summarise performance at the end of a run
#'
#' @param truth_history List of integer vectors (incidence per turn).
#' @param observed_history Tibble of observed results (available outcomes).
#' @param pop_tbl Population tibble with `pop` column.
#' @param total_spend Numeric total spend accumulated across turns.
#' @return Named list of metrics.
#' @export
# Rt from a case series --------------------------------------------------------
#
# In this game one turn is one generation: each case's infections appear the
# next turn, so the serial interval is exactly 1 turn. Rt over a window of
# turns is then (cases in the window) / (cases one turn earlier), with
# uncertainty from Cori et al.'s method. (Assuming a longer serial interval, as an earlier
# version did, overstates Rt: 2.3 for a series growing 1.3x per turn.)
#
# Windows with fewer than `min_cases` cases the turn before give NA rather
# than a number driven by the prior.
estimate_rt_table <- function(incid_vector, window = 3, min_cases = 5) {
  incid_vector <- as.numeric(incid_vector)
  incid_vector[is.na(incid_vector)] <- 0
  n <- length(incid_vector)
  if (n < window + 1) {
    return(tibble::tibble(t_end = integer(), mean = numeric(), lower = numeric(), upper = numeric()))
  }

  t_end <- seq(window + 1, n)
  t_start <- t_end - window + 1

  # Cori et al. (2013), as in EpiEstim, with a 1-turn serial interval: the
  # posterior for R over a window is a gamma distribution with
  #   shape = prior shape + cases in the window
  #   rate  = 1 / prior scale + cases one turn earlier (the infectors)
  # and EpiEstim's default prior (mean 5, sd 5: shape 1, scale 5).
  # Matches EpiEstim::estimate_R(method = "non_parametric_si",
  # si_distr = c(0, 1)) exactly, without the package.
  prior_shape <- 1
  prior_scale <- 5

  cases <- vapply(seq_along(t_start), function(i) sum(incid_vector[t_start[i]:t_end[i]]), numeric(1))
  infectors <- vapply(seq_along(t_start), function(i) sum(incid_vector[(t_start[i] - 1):(t_end[i] - 1)]), numeric(1))

  shape <- prior_shape + cases
  scale <- 1 / (1 / prior_scale + infectors)

  # too few infectors to judge: no estimate rather than one driven by the prior
  enough <- infectors >= min_cases

  tibble::tibble(
    t_end = t_end,
    mean = ifelse(enough, shape * scale, NA_real_),
    lower = ifelse(enough, stats::qgamma(0.025, shape = shape, scale = scale), NA_real_),
    upper = ifelse(enough, stats::qgamma(0.975, shape = shape, scale = scale), NA_real_)
  )
}

# Latest Rt estimate from a case series (see estimate_rt_table())
estimate_rt_series <- function(incid_vector, ...) {
  tbl <- estimate_rt_table(incid_vector, ...)
  if (nrow(tbl) == 0) {
    return(list(mean = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  }
  last <- tbl[nrow(tbl), ]
  list(mean = last$mean, lower = last$lower, upper = last$upper)
}

# Positives per turn, with every turn present (0 where nothing came back)
positives_by_turn <- function(observed_history, last_turn = NULL) {
  turns <- observed_history$turn_available
  if (is.null(last_turn)) {
    last_turn <- if (length(turns) == 0) 0 else max(turns)
  }
  counts <- numeric(last_turn + 1)
  if (length(turns) > 0) {
    by_turn <- tapply(observed_history$positives, turns, sum)
    counts[as.integer(names(by_turn)) + 1] <- by_turn
  }
  counts
}

score_run <- function(truth_history, observed_history, pop_tbl, total_spend = 0) {
  if (length(truth_history) == 0) {
    stop("truth_history must contain at least one turn")
  }

  truth_mat <- do.call(rbind, truth_history)
  total_incidence <- rowSums(truth_mat)
  peak_true <- max(total_incidence)

  final_truth <- truth_mat[nrow(truth_mat), ]
  true_prev_rate <- sum(final_truth) / sum(pop_tbl$pop)

  # first REAL case found by the player's own tests (not the free starter
  # alert, not a false positive)
  own_tests <- observed_history
  if ("source" %in% names(own_tests)) {
    own_tests <- own_tests[is.na(own_tests$source) | own_tests$source != "starter", , drop = FALSE]
  }
  real_found <- if ("true_pos" %in% names(own_tests)) own_tests$true_pos else own_tests$positives
  detection_turns <- own_tests$turn_available[real_found > 0]
  time_to_detection <- if (length(detection_turns) == 0 || all(is.na(detection_turns))) {
    NA_integer_
  } else {
    min(detection_turns, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  if (is.infinite(time_to_detection)) {
    time_to_detection <- NA_integer_
  }

  observed_turns <- observed_history |>
    dplyr::group_by(turn_available) |>
    dplyr::summarise(positives = sum(positives), .groups = "drop")
  peak_observed <- if (nrow(observed_turns) == 0) 0 else max(observed_turns$positives)

  total_tests <- sum(observed_history$n)
  total_pos <- sum(observed_history$positives)
  pct_positive <- if (total_tests == 0) NA_real_ else 100 * total_pos / total_tests

  n_turns <- nrow(truth_mat)
  n_boros <- ncol(truth_mat)

  truth_df <- tibble::tibble(
    turn = rep(seq_len(n_turns) - 1L, each = n_boros),
    borough_index = rep(seq_len(n_boros), times = n_turns),
    true_prev = as.numeric(t(truth_mat)) / rep(pop_tbl$pop, times = n_turns)
  )

  inferred_df <- observed_history |>
    dplyr::group_by(turn_sampled, borough_index) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      tests = sum(n),
      positives = sum(positives),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      inferred = ifelse(tests == 0, 0, (positives + 1) / (tests + 2))
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(turn = turn_sampled)

  calib_df <- truth_df |>
    dplyr::left_join(inferred_df, by = c("turn", "borough_index"))

  calib_df$inferred[is.na(calib_df$inferred)] <- 0
  calib_df$tests[is.na(calib_df$tests)] <- 0

  turn_metrics <- calib_df |>
    dplyr::group_by(turn) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      rmse = sqrt(mean((true_prev - inferred)^2)),
      tests = sum(tests, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  if (nrow(turn_metrics) == 0) {
    calibration_gap <- NA_real_
  } else if (sum(turn_metrics$tests, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    calibration_gap <- stats::weighted.mean(turn_metrics$rmse, w = turn_metrics$tests, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    calibration_gap <- mean(turn_metrics$rmse, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  observed_rt <- estimate_rt_series(positives_by_turn(observed_history, last_turn = n_turns - 1))
  truth_rt <- estimate_rt_series(total_incidence)

  # how many real cases the player's tests found, and how many of their
  # positives were false
  real_cases_found <- if ("true_pos" %in% names(own_tests)) sum(own_tests$true_pos) else NA_real_
  own_positives <- sum(own_tests$positives)
  false_positives <- if (is.na(real_cases_found)) NA_real_ else own_positives - real_cases_found
  total_true_infections <- sum(total_incidence)

  list(
    time_to_detection = time_to_detection,
    real_cases_found = real_cases_found,
    share_of_infections_found = if (total_true_infections > 0) real_cases_found / total_true_infections else NA_real_,
    total_true_infections = total_true_infections,
    own_positives = own_positives,
    false_positives = false_positives,
    peak_true_incidence = peak_true,
    peak_observed_positives = peak_observed,
    percent_positive = pct_positive,
    total_spend = total_spend,
    calibration_gap = calibration_gap,
    true_prevalence_rate = true_prev_rate,
    rt_observed_mean = observed_rt$mean,
    rt_observed_lower = observed_rt$lower,
    rt_observed_upper = observed_rt$upper,
    rt_truth_mean = truth_rt$mean,
    rt_truth_lower = truth_rt$lower,
    rt_truth_upper = truth_rt$upper
  )
}

#' Assemble a run report containing metrics and turn-by-turn details
#'
#' @param truth_history List of integer vectors (incidence per turn).
#' @param observed_history Tibble of observed results (available outcomes).
#' @param pop_tbl Population tibble with `pop` column.
#' @param total_spend Numeric total spend accumulated across turns.
#' @param run_log Tibble of per-turn summaries captured during gameplay.
#' @param truth_log Truth log tibble (e.g., from `append_truth_log()`), used for derived stats like imports.
#' @return List with `metrics` and `turn_summary` tibble.
#' @export
build_run_report <- function(truth_history, observed_history, pop_tbl, total_spend = 0, run_log = tibble::tibble(), truth_log = tibble::tibble()) {
  metrics <- score_run(
    truth_history = truth_history,
    observed_history = observed_history,
    pop_tbl = pop_tbl,
    total_spend = total_spend
  )

  if (!is.null(truth_log) && nrow(truth_log) > 0 && "cumulative" %in% names(truth_log)) {
    final_turn <- max(truth_log$turn, na.rm = TRUE)
    final_cumulative <- truth_log |>
      dplyr::filter(turn == final_turn) |>
      dplyr::summarise(total_cumulative = sum(cumulative, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
      dplyr::pull(total_cumulative)
    pop_total <- sum(pop_tbl$pop, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (is.finite(final_cumulative) && is.finite(pop_total) && pop_total > 0) {
      metrics$true_prevalence_rate <- final_cumulative / pop_total
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(truth_log) && nrow(truth_log) > 0 && "cumulative_deaths" %in% names(truth_log)) {
    final_turn <- max(truth_log$turn, na.rm = TRUE)
    final_deaths <- truth_log |>
      dplyr::filter(turn == final_turn) |>
      dplyr::summarise(total_deaths = sum(cumulative_deaths, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
      dplyr::pull(total_deaths)
    if (is.finite(final_deaths)) {
      metrics$total_deaths <- final_deaths
    }
  }

  truth_totals <- vapply(truth_history, sum, numeric(1))
  true_hotspots <- vapply(truth_history, function(x) sum(x > 0), integer(1))
  turns <- seq_along(truth_totals) - 1L

  truth_df <- tibble::tibble(
    turn = turns,
    truth_total = truth_totals,
    boroughs_with_cases = true_hotspots
  )

  observed_df <- observed_history |>
    dplyr::group_by(turn_available) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      observed_tests = sum(n),
      observed_positives = sum(positives),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(turn = turn_available)

  imports_df <- if (!is.null(truth_log) && nrow(truth_log) > 0) {
    truth_log |>
      dplyr::group_by(turn) |>
      dplyr::summarise(imports_total = sum(imports), .groups = "drop")
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(turn = integer(), imports_total = integer())
  }

  deaths_df <- if (!is.null(truth_log) && nrow(truth_log) > 0 && "deaths" %in% names(truth_log)) {
    truth_log |>
      dplyr::group_by(turn) |>
      dplyr::summarise(deaths_total = sum(deaths), .groups = "drop")
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(turn = integer(), deaths_total = integer())
  }

  log_clean <- run_log
  if (nrow(log_clean) == 0) {
    log_clean <- tibble::tibble(turn = integer())
  } else {
    log_clean <- log_clean |>
      dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("truth_total", "observed_tests", "observed_positives", "imports_total")))
  }

  turn_summary <- truth_df |>
    dplyr::left_join(observed_df, by = "turn") |>
    dplyr::left_join(imports_df, by = "turn") |>
    dplyr::left_join(deaths_df, by = "turn") |>
    dplyr::left_join(log_clean, by = "turn") |>
    dplyr::arrange(turn)

  numeric_defaults <- c(
    observed_tests = 0,
    observed_positives = 0,
    imports_total = 0,
    deaths_total = 0,
    tests_ag = 0,
    tests_pcr = 0,
    allocation_spend = 0,
    intervention_cost = 0,
    total_turn_spend = 0,
    cumulative_spend = 0,
    queue_pending = 0
  )

  for (field in names(numeric_defaults)) {
    if (field %in% names(turn_summary)) {
      turn_summary[[field]][is.na(turn_summary[[field]])] <- numeric_defaults[[field]]
    }
  }

  if ("total_turn_spend" %in% names(turn_summary)) {
    turn_summary$cumulative_spend <- cumsum(turn_summary$total_turn_spend)
  }

  if ("active_interventions" %in% names(turn_summary)) {
    turn_summary$active_interventions[is.na(turn_summary$active_interventions) | turn_summary$active_interventions == ""] <- "None"
  }

  if ("notes" %in% names(turn_summary)) {
    turn_summary$notes[is.na(turn_summary$notes)] <- ""
  }

  list(
    metrics = metrics,
    turn_summary = turn_summary
  )
}

# Strategy bots ----------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each bot plays the game the way a student following one strategy would.
# A bot only gets player_view() (what a student can see), never the truth.
#
# A bot is function(view, memory) returning list(actions, memory).
# `memory` lets a bot remember things between turns (starts as list()).
#
# Bots use whichever control levers the current game offers, so they keep
# working as new levers are added.

# Helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Positives and tests per borough in results returned over the last `window` turns
recent_results <- function(view, window = 2) {
  n_b <- nrow(view$pop_tbl)

  history <- view$history
  recent <- history$turn_available >= view$turn - window

  positives <- integer(n_b)
  tests <- integer(n_b)
  if (any(recent)) {
    by_boro <- rowsum(cbind(history$positives[recent], history$n[recent]), history$borough_index[recent])
    idx <- as.integer(rownames(by_boro))
    positives[idx] <- by_boro[, 1]
    tests[idx] <- by_boro[, 2]
  }

  list(positives = positives, tests = tests)
}

# Boroughs whose positivity is clearly above what false positives alone
# would give (a crude "is this signal real?" check)
signal_boroughs <- function(view, window = 2, type_spec = NULL) {
  res <- recent_results(view, window)

  # worst-case false positive rate across the tests in use
  spec <- type_spec %||% min(unlist(view$spec))
  fp_rate <- 1 - spec

  expected_fp <- res$tests * fp_rate
  # signal = more positives than false positives could plausibly explain
  which(res$positives >= 2 & res$positives > expected_fp + 2 * sqrt(expected_fp + 1))
}

# Money left for tests after the chosen interventions and local restrictions
test_budget <- function(view, interventions, restricted = integer()) {
  cost <- sum(view$interventions$cost[view$interventions$id %in% interventions])
  cost <- cost + sum(view$local_costs[restricted])
  max(0, (view$allowance %||% view$budget) - cost)
}

# Keep only as many boroughs (in the order given) as the allowance can pay
# to restrict, leaving `keep_for_tests` of the allowance for testing
affordable_restrictions <- function(view, boroughs, keep_for_tests = 0.3) {
  money <- (view$allowance %||% view$budget) * (1 - keep_for_tests)
  costs <- view$local_costs[boroughs]
  boroughs <- boroughs[cumsum(costs) <= money]

  # no more than the share of people that can be restricted at once
  share <- view$restriction_share
  if (!is.null(share) && length(boroughs) > 0) {
    pop <- view$pop_tbl$pop
    covered <- cumsum(pop[boroughs]) / sum(pop)
    boroughs <- boroughs[covered <= share | seq_along(boroughs) == 1]
  }
  boroughs
}

# Spread a number of tests across boroughs in proportion to weights
spread_tests <- function(n_tests, weights) {
  weights <- weights / sum(weights)
  floor(n_tests * weights)
}

# Build an allocation table
make_allocations <- function(view, n_ag = 0L, n_pcr = 0L) {
  n_b <- nrow(view$pop_tbl)
  data.frame(
    borough_index = seq_len(n_b),
    borough_name = view$pop_tbl$borough_name,
    n_ag = as.integer(rep_len(n_ag, n_b)),
    n_pcr = as.integer(rep_len(n_pcr, n_b)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# The bots ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Chase the signal: pour tests (and any local controls) into wherever
#    positives turn up; follow the starter alert until then.
bot_chase <- function(view, memory) {
  res <- recent_results(view, window = 1)

  if (sum(res$positives) > 0) {
    target <- which.max(res$positives)
  } else if (!is.null(memory$target)) {
    target <- memory$target
  } else {
    target <- view$alerted
  }
  if (is.na(target)) {
    target <- sample.int(nrow(view$pop_tbl), 1)
  }
  memory$target <- target

  # 70% of tests in the target, 30% shared across its neighbours
  neighbours <- which(view$A[target, ] > 0)
  weights <- numeric(nrow(view$pop_tbl))
  weights[target] <- 0.7
  weights[neighbours] <- 0.3 / max(1, length(neighbours))

  # respond once positives are seen: lock down the target borough
  restricted <- if (sum(res$positives) > 0) affordable_restrictions(view, target) else integer()

  # cheapest fast test available
  money <- test_budget(view, character(), restricted)
  if (view$testing$ag_available) {
    n_ag <- spread_tests(money / view$costs$ag, weights)
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_ag = n_ag)
  } else {
    n_pcr <- spread_tests(money / view$costs$pcr, weights)
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_pcr = n_pcr)
  }

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = allocs,
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = character(),
      local_restrictions = restricted
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 2. Broad surveillance: random sample across all boroughs every turn, act
#    once the signal rises above the false-positive noise.
bot_broad <- function(view, memory) {
  # restrict boroughs where the signal is clearly real, strongest first
  signal <- signal_boroughs(view, window = 2)
  res <- recent_results(view, window = 2)
  signal <- signal[order(-res$positives[signal])]
  restricted <- affordable_restrictions(view, signal, keep_for_tests = 0.5)

  # cheap fast antigen if it exists (accepting false positives), else PCR,
  # spread by population
  money <- test_budget(view, character(), restricted)
  if (view$testing$ag_available) {
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_ag = spread_tests(money / view$costs$ag, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  } else {
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_pcr = spread_tests(money / view$costs$pcr, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  }

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = allocs,
      sampling_mode = "random",
      interventions = character(),
      local_restrictions = restricted
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 3. Test, trace, isolate: steady symptomatic PCR testing everywhere, plus
#    contact tracing.
bot_tti <- function(view, memory) {
  interventions <- character()
  tracing_cost <- view$tracing_cost %||% 0

  money <- test_budget(view, interventions) - tracing_cost
  n_pcr <- spread_tests(max(0, money) / view$costs$pcr, view$pop_tbl$pop)

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = make_allocations(view, n_pcr = n_pcr),
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = interventions,
      tracing = TRUE
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 4. Build testing first: keep investing in better testing until the top
#    level, testing symptomatic people widely with whatever exists meanwhile.
bot_build <- function(view, memory) {
  build <- isTRUE(view$testing$can_build)
  develop <- isTRUE(view$testing$can_develop_rapid)
  paying_rapid <- develop || isTRUE(view$testing$developing_rapid)
  money <- test_budget(view, character()) -
    (if (build) view$testing$build_cost else 0) - (if (paying_rapid) view$testing$rapid_cost else 0)
  if (money < 0 && build) {
    # cannot afford both this report: keep developing rapid tests
    build <- FALSE
    money <- test_budget(view, character()) - (if (paying_rapid) view$testing$rapid_cost else 0)
  }

  allocs <- if (view$testing$ag_available) {
    make_allocations(view, n_ag = spread_tests(max(0, money) / view$costs$ag, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  } else {
    make_allocations(view, n_pcr = spread_tests(max(0, money) / view$costs$pcr, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  }

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = allocs,
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = character(),
      build_testing = build,
      develop_rapid = develop
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 5. Hit hard early: London-wide measures from turn 0, spend little on tests.
bot_hit_hard <- function(view, memory) {
  interventions <- "distancing"

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = make_allocations(view),
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = interventions
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 5b. All-in early: like Hit hard early, but spends the full per-turn amount
#     from turn 0 (London-wide measures plus wide symptomatic testing) with no
#     pacing, until the money runs out.
bot_all_in <- function(view, memory) {
  interventions <- "distancing"

  # spend everything allowed this turn, not a fair share of what is left
  money <- view$budget - sum(view$interventions$cost[view$interventions$id %in% interventions])
  if (money < 0) {
    # cannot even pay for the measures any more
    return(list(actions = list(), memory = memory))
  }

  if (view$testing$ag_available) {
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_ag = spread_tests(money / view$costs$ag, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  } else {
    allocs <- make_allocations(view, n_pcr = spread_tests(money / view$costs$pcr, view$pop_tbl$pop))
  }

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = allocs,
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = interventions
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# 6. Respond to hospital reports (formerly "Watch and wait"): no testing; rely on hospital reports and restrict the
#    boroughs where admissions turn up.
bot_hospital_reports <- function(view, memory) {
  recent <- view$reports |>
    dplyr::filter(turn >= view$turn - 1) |>
    dplyr::group_by(borough_index) |>
    dplyr::summarise(admissions = sum(admissions), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::filter(admissions > 0) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(admissions))

  restricted <- affordable_restrictions(view, recent$borough_index, keep_for_tests = 0)

  list(
    actions = list(
      allocations = make_allocations(view),
      sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
      interventions = character(),
      local_restrictions = restricted
    ),
    memory = memory
  )
}

# Reference: do nothing at all. Every strategy is scored against this on the
# same outbreak. Not shown as a strategy.
bot_do_nothing <- function(view, memory) {
  list(actions = list(), memory = memory)
}

# Adaptive strategies --------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These read the data each report and change course, the way a sensible
# response team would. They only see what a player sees.

# Areas with hospital admissions in the last two reports, most first
hospital_cluster_areas <- function(view) {
  rep <- view$reports
  if (is.null(rep) || nrow(rep) == 0) return(integer())
  recent <- rep[rep$turn >= view$turn - 1 & rep$admissions > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(recent) == 0) return(integer())
  by_area <- tapply(recent$admissions, recent$borough_index, sum)
  as.integer(names(sort(by_area, decreasing = TRUE)))
}

# Growth per report in hospital admissions (Rt from admissions, per report)
admissions_growth <- function(view) {
  rep <- view$reports
  if (is.null(rep) || nrow(rep) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  per_turn <- tapply(rep$admissions, factor(rep$turn, levels = 0:max(rep$turn)), sum)
  per_turn[is.na(per_turn)] <- 0
  estimate_rt_series(as.numeric(per_turn))$mean
}

# Tests for this report: what is left after the measures, on the best test
# available, never more than labs or kits can handle, in the given areas
# (everywhere if none)
adaptive_tests <- function(view, money, areas = integer()) {
  use_ag <- isTRUE(view$testing$ag_available)
  per_test <- if (use_ag) view$costs$ag else view$costs$pcr
  limit <- if (use_ag) view$testing$ag_capacity else view$testing$capacity
  n <- min(max(0, money) / per_test, limit)
  weights <- view$pop_tbl$pop
  if (length(areas) > 0) weights <- ifelse(seq_along(weights) %in% areas, weights, 0)
  tests <- spread_tests(n, weights)
  if (use_ag) make_allocations(view, n_ag = tests) else make_allocations(view, n_pcr = tests)
}

measures_cost <- function(view, interventions = character(), restricted = integer(), tracing = FALSE,
                          rapid = FALSE) {
  sum(view$interventions$cost[view$interventions$id %in% interventions]) +
    sum(view$local_costs[restricted]) +
    (if (tracing) view$tracing_cost else 0) +
    (if (rapid) view$testing$rapid_cost else 0)
}

# A. Act on hospital clusters: restrict the areas with recent hospital cases,
#    trace known cases, and test the sick in those areas
bot_hospital_clusters <- function(view, memory) {
  areas <- hospital_cluster_areas(view)
  restricted <- affordable_restrictions(view, areas, keep_for_tests = 0.4)
  tracing <- TRUE
  money <- view$allowance - measures_cost(view, restricted = restricted, tracing = tracing)
  list(actions = list(allocations = adaptive_tests(view, money, areas), sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
                      local_restrictions = restricted, tracing = tracing), memory = memory)
}

# B. Escalate when it grows: test the sick and trace; lock down once allowed
#    and admissions are growing; lift it when they fall
bot_escalate <- function(view, memory) {
  growth <- admissions_growth(view)
  locked <- isTRUE(memory$locked)
  if (!locked && isTRUE(view$lockdown_allowed) && !is.na(growth) && growth > 1.2) locked <- TRUE
  if (locked && !is.na(growth) && growth < 0.9) locked <- FALSE
  memory$locked <- locked
  interventions <- if (locked) "distancing" else character()
  money <- view$allowance - measures_cost(view, interventions, tracing = TRUE)
  list(actions = list(allocations = adaptive_tests(view, money), sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
                      interventions = interventions, tracing = TRUE), memory = memory)
}

# C. Invest, then test widely: develop rapid tests at once, test the sick
#    everywhere, trace known cases
bot_invest_then_test <- function(view, memory) {
  develop <- isTRUE(view$testing$can_develop_rapid)
  paying <- develop || isTRUE(view$testing$developing_rapid)
  money <- view$allowance - measures_cost(view, tracing = TRUE, rapid = paying)
  list(actions = list(allocations = adaptive_tests(view, money), sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
                      tracing = TRUE, develop_rapid = develop), memory = memory)
}

# D. Everything, adaptively: rapid tests, tracing and restricting hospital
#    clusters, and a lockdown once hospital beds are half full
bot_everything <- function(view, memory) {
  develop <- isTRUE(view$testing$can_develop_rapid)
  paying <- develop || isTRUE(view$testing$developing_rapid)
  interventions <- if (isTRUE(view$lockdown_allowed) && view$bed_pressure >= 0.5) "distancing" else character()
  areas <- hospital_cluster_areas(view)
  restricted <- affordable_restrictions(view, areas, keep_for_tests = 0.5)
  money <- view$allowance - measures_cost(view, interventions, restricted, tracing = TRUE, rapid = paying)
  if (money < 0) {
    restricted <- integer()
    money <- view$allowance - measures_cost(view, interventions, tracing = TRUE, rapid = paying)
  }
  list(actions = list(allocations = adaptive_tests(view, money, areas), sampling_mode = "symptomatic",
                      interventions = interventions, local_restrictions = restricted, tracing = TRUE,
                      develop_rapid = develop), memory = memory)
}

strategy_bots <- function() {
  list(
    "Chase the signal" = bot_chase,
    "Broad surveillance" = bot_broad,
    "Test, trace, isolate" = bot_tti,
    "Build testing first" = bot_build,
    "Hit hard early" = bot_hit_hard,
    "All-in early" = bot_all_in,
    "Respond to hospital reports" = bot_hospital_reports,
    "Act on hospital clusters" = bot_hospital_clusters,
    "Escalate when it grows" = bot_escalate,
    "Invest, then test widely" = bot_invest_then_test,
    "Everything, adaptively" = bot_everything
  )
}

# Play a whole game with one bot ------------------------------------------------

play_bot_game <- function(config, bot, seed, n_turns = 20L) {
  state <- new_game(config, seed = seed)
  memory <- list()

  for (i in seq_len(n_turns)) {
    view <- player_view(state, config)
    choice <- bot(view, memory)
    memory <- choice$memory

    result <- play_turn(state, choice$actions, config)
    if (!result$ok) {
      # over budget: play the turn doing nothing instead
      result <- play_turn(state, list(), config)
    }
    state <- result$state

    # the response ends by itself once the outbreak is declared over
    if (declared_over(state, config)) break
  }

  history <- state$truth$history

  # infections and deaths during the response (what happened before the
  # first report is the same whatever the player does)
  deaths_eventual <- eventual_deaths(state$truth, config) - (state$start_deaths_eventual %||% 0)

  list(
    cumulative_infections = sum(state$truth$cumulative) - (state$start_infections %||% 0),
    final_incidence = sum(history[[length(history)]]),
    deaths = sum(state$truth$cumulative_deaths),
    deaths_eventual = deaths_eventual,
    extra_deaths_no_bed = sum(state$hospital$extra_deaths),
    peak_bed_use = if (length(state$hospital$occupancy)) max(state$hospital$occupancy) / config$tp$hospital$beds else 0,
    spend = state$spend_total,
    state = state
  )
}

# Teaching parameters ----------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every value that controls game balance lives here, so the difficulty and the
# "ways the data can mislead you" can be tuned in one place before a class.
#
# Each block says which trap it sets up for students.

teaching_params <- function() {
  list(

    # New Game draws a fresh random outbreak by default, so students cannot
    # memorise where it starts from a previous round. Untick "Random" in the
    # app (or set this to FALSE) to give a whole class the same outbreak.
    random_seed_default = TRUE,

    # Money is in a made-up unit so it does not suggest any real country's
    # prices. Change the name here to change it everywhere.
    currency = "credits",

    # All money and capacity values below are set for London (33 boroughs,
    # about 9.1 million people). In another place they are scaled by its
    # population (a bigger place has a bigger health budget, more labs and
    # beds), and imports by its number of areas. See scale_to_place().
    reference_pop = 9089736,

    # The outbreak starts unseen, from one infected person, and is noticed
    # when a cluster of severe illness turns up: `admissions` hospital
    # admissions in total, or the first death. An outbreak that dies out
    # before that is never noticed, so a new one is drawn. Mild, fast
    # spreaders are bigger by the time anyone notices; deadly ones are
    # noticed early. The report comes from where the patients are, not
    # necessarily where it started.
    # Trap: the first case found is not the first case.
    head_start = list(admissions = 3L, index_cases = 1L, max_reports = 104L),

    # The outbreak is declared over (and the response ends by itself) after
    # this many reports in a row with no hospital admissions and no deaths
    # reported. Calibrated in sim/checks/calibrate_declared_over.R: right
    # (it never comes back) 97% of the time across all diseases; silent
    # polio-like is the exception. Test positives do not count: false
    # positives never stop while anyone tests.
    declare_over_after = 6L,

    # Reports until the reference lab identifies the disease (then its name
    # is shown). Before that, students have to judge it from the data.
    identify_after = 6L,

    # Days between reports (one turn). Every disease is played at this
    # cadence: 7 = a weekly report, 1 = daily. Spread, hospital and death
    # delays are converted from the disease's own timescale (scenarios.R).
    # Money, lab capacity, test delays and measure lags below are per report.
    report_days = 7L,

    # Date the first patient is reported (day 0). Day 1 is the first turn.
    start_date = "2027-10-04",
    reference_units = 33L,

    # Starter intel: an early alert sends 200 antigen tests to one borough.
    # The alert is only right some of the time; otherwise it points at a
    # borough picked at random (a false alarm).
    # Trap: early signals and rumours can send you to the wrong place.
    starter_alert = list(
      tests = 200L,
      accuracy = 0.6
    ),

    # Test performance, delays and costs.
    # Antigen is cheap and fast but its specificity is lower than PCR, so
    # mass antigen testing where prevalence is low produces mostly false
    # positives.
    # Trap: positive predictive value depends on how common the infection is.
    tests = list(
      sens = list(ag = 0.80, pcr = 0.98),
      spec = list(ag = 0.98, pcr = 0.999),
      delays = list(ag = 0L, pcr = 1L),
      costs = list(ag = 2, pcr = 10),
      budget = 300000,        # most that can be spent in one report (credits)
      prev_floor = 1e-6
    ),

    # Detection window: a test stays positive for a while after infection,
    # so a random sample finds people infected over the last few turns, not
    # just this turn (PCR picks up old infections for longer than antigen).
    # Only the ones infected this turn are still spreading, so only they
    # count for isolation. Symptomatic testing finds people who are sick
    # now, so it is not affected.
    # Trap: lots of positives can mean an outbreak that has already passed.
    detection_window = list(ag = 2L, pcr = 3L),

    # One pot of money for the whole outbreak, and how long the game lasts.
    # Spending big early leaves less for later.
    # Trap: you cannot both see everything and control everything.
    game_turns = 20L,
    budget_total = 2400000,

    # Isolation of confirmed cases.
    # Every true case found by a test is isolated, cutting onward spread.
    # How much survives a slow result depends on the disease (delay_decay
    # in scenarios.R), and cases found through symptomatic testing have
    # already done their pre-symptom spreading (presymptomatic).
    # Trap: a slow result finds a case after it has already spread.
    isolation = list(
      effectiveness = 0.8,
      # Isolation gets harder to support as positives pile up (checks,
      # support payments, enforcement, households). At `half_strength_load`
      # positives a turn, each isolation works half as well. Every positive
      # counts, real or false.
      half_strength_load = 2000
    ),

    # Hospital capacity.
    # A London-wide pool of beds for this disease. Patients stay `stay_turns`.
    # When more patients need a bed than there are beds, the share without a
    # proper bed die at an extra rate, and hospitals under pressure report
    # fewer admissions. Hospitals publish how full they are.
    # Set at a teaching level (not real bed numbers): severe diseases fill
    # it if left alone, mild ones do not.
    # Trap: "wait for the hospital data" is fine until hospitals are full.
    hospital = list(
      beds = 600,
      stay_turns = 2L,
      death_if_no_bed = 0.3,
      reporting_drop_when_full = 0.5
    ),

    # Reports that arrive whatever the player does: hospital admissions and
    # deaths. Admissions are reported where the hospital is (usually, not
    # always, the patient's own borough), some time after infection, and
    # not all are recognised as this disease.
    # Trap: hospital data is late, incomplete and in the wrong place.
    reports = list(
      hosp_delay = 3L,        # fallback only: each disease sets its own (scenarios.R)
      hosp_ascertainment = 0.8,
      own_borough = 0.5,
      death_ascertainment = 0.9
    ),

    # Testing.
    # PCR comes in two levels (set per disease in scenarios.R): a reference
    # lab only, or hospital labs (cheaper, more capacity). "Improve PCR"
    # moves up a level: a lump sum, a few reports, and half capacity while
    # staff are diverted. capacity = PCR tests the labs can process per
    # report across London; more than that joins a backlog and comes back
    # late. PCR results always come back with the next report.
    # Trap: ordering more tests than labs can process makes every result late.
    test_levels = tibble::tibble(
      level = 1:2,
      label = c("Reference lab only", "Hospital labs"),
      pcr_cost = c(40, 20),
      pcr_delay = c(1L, 1L),
      capacity = c(2000, 6000)
    ),
    build_testing = list(
      cost = 150000,
      turns = 3L,
      capacity_while_building = 0.5
    ),

    # Rapid antigen tests do not exist for a new disease: they have to be
    # developed, paying `cost` every report for `turns` reports. Then they are cheap,
    # instant and plentiful (`kits` a report), and because people can test
    # themselves at home, a lockdown works better (`lockdown_Rt_multiplier`
    # replaces social distancing's usual effect).
    # Trap: invest now in a tool you can only use later.
    rapid_tests = list(
      cost = 40000,       # per report while being developed
      turns = 8L,
      ag_cost = 2,
      kits = 60000,
      lockdown_Rt_multiplier = 0.4
    ),

    # National public health agency: every report it tests the same number of
    # people with symptoms, spread across all areas by population, free to
    # the player: a positivity figure that does not move when the player
    # changes their own testing. The agency's Rt comes from hospital
    # admissions (a fixed share of cases, whatever anyone tests), the
    # steadiest signal. Information only (nobody is isolated because of it).
    sentinel = list(tests = 1000),

    # Contact tracing.
    # A team that follows up known cases and quarantines their contacts,
    # removing some of the people each case has already infected. Known
    # cases are your positive tests and the admissions hospitals report
    # (which cost nothing to find, but are found late: an admission was
    # infected hosp_delay ago, so for a fast disease its contacts have long
    # moved on). Limited capacity per turn.
    # Trap: tracing looks great when cases are few (an early Ebola-like
    # outbreak), then silently fails when cases outnumber tracers (and you
    # cannot see the ones you never found).
    tracing = list(
      cost = 40000,          # per turn while switched on
      capacity = 400,        # known cases followed up per report
      effectiveness = 0.5,   # share of each case's onward infections caught
      contacts_per_case = 10 # people named and checked for each case (for the report)
    ),

    # Local restrictions on single boroughs.
    # Infected people in a restricted borough pass it on less (anywhere).
    # Much cheaper than London-wide measures, but only useful in the right
    # place. Cost scales with the borough's population. Same lag/fatigue
    # rules as the London-wide interventions.
    # Only `max_pop_share` of the population can be under local restrictions
    # at once (always at least one area): police, support and goodwill run
    # out, so you have to choose which clusters matter most.
    # Trap: acting hard on an early positive is great if it was the origin,
    # wasted if it was a false positive or a side branch.
    local_restrictions = list(
      max_pop_share = 0.1,
      Rt_multiplier = 0.3,
      cost_per_100k = 9000,
      lag = 1L,
      fatigue = 0.9
    ),

    # Symptomatic testing pool.
    # Testing people with symptoms finds more cases than random testing, but
    # (1) people in some boroughs are less likely to come forward for a test
    #     (hidden care-seeking multiplier, drawn fresh each game), and
    # (2) a wave of some other respiratory illness swells the number of
    #     people with symptoms partway through the game, diluting positivity.
    # Random testing is unaffected by both but finds far fewer cases.
    # Traps: who gets tested shapes the map; positivity can fall while
    # infections rise.
    symptomatic = list(
      pool_frac = 0.005,               # share of population seeking a test each turn (baseline);
                                       # symptomatic tests per borough are capped at this many people
      care_seeking_range = c(0.3, 1.5), # per-borough multiplier, uniform draw
      wave_height = 2,                 # pool grows to (1 + height) x baseline at peak
      wave_width = 2,                  # turns (sd of a Gaussian bump)
      wave_peak_range = c(4L, 12L)      # peak turn, drawn each game
    ),

    # Interventions.
    # Each one costs budget every turn it is ticked, only starts working the
    # turn after it is switched on (lag), and some lose effect the longer
    # they run (fatigue: effect multiplied by `fatigue` each extra turn).
    # Once switched off, the fading wears off one report per report.
    # Social distancing (lockdown) is only possible once the public would
    # accept it: after `lockdown_trigger$deaths` reported deaths, or with
    # hospital beds `lockdown_trigger$bed_share` full.
    lockdown_trigger = list(deaths = 10, bed_share = 0.25),

    # Traps: you cannot judge an intervention on the turn you start it, and
    # money spent on control is money not spent on seeing the outbreak.
    interventions = tibble::tibble(
      id = "distancing",
      label = "Social distancing",
      cost = 150000,
      Rt_multiplier = 0.5,
      imports_multiplier = 1,
      ag_delay_adjust = 0,
      pcr_delay_adjust = 0,
      lag = 1L,
      fatigue = 0.8
    )
  )
}

# Draw the hidden biases for one game -----------------------------------------

draw_game_biases <- function(n_boroughs, params = teaching_params()) {
  sym <- params$symptomatic

  care_seeking <- stats::runif(
    n_boroughs,
    min = sym$care_seeking_range[1],
    max = sym$care_seeking_range[2]
  )

  wave_peak <- sample(
    seq(sym$wave_peak_range[1], sym$wave_peak_range[2]),
    size = 1
  )

  list(
    care_seeking = care_seeking,
    wave_peak = wave_peak
  )
}

# Size of the symptomatic pool on a given turn ---------------------------------

symptomatic_pool_frac <- function(turn, wave_peak, params = teaching_params()) {
  sym <- params$symptomatic

  # Gaussian bump centred on the wave peak
  bump <- exp(-((turn - wave_peak)^2) / (2 * sym$wave_width^2))

  sym$pool_frac * (1 + sym$wave_height * bump)
}

# Format an amount of money for display, e.g. "60,000 credits" -----------------

format_money <- function(x) {
  paste(format_round(x), teaching_params()$currency)
}

# A round, readable number: 77,460 -> "80,000" (see nice_round())
format_round <- function(x) {
  format(nice_round(x), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
}

# Turn logging utilities ----------------------------------------------------

#' Initialise empty turn-by-turn logs
#'
#' @param pop_tbl Population table with columns `borough_name`, `gss_code`, and `pop`.
#' @return A list with empty tibbles for truth, observations, and actions.
#' @export
init_turn_logs <- function(pop_tbl) {
  required_cols <- c("borough_name", "gss_code", "pop")
  if (!all(required_cols %in% names(pop_tbl))) {
    stop("pop_tbl must contain columns: ", paste(required_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  pop_tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(pop_tbl)
  pop_tbl <- pop_tbl |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      borough_index = dplyr::row_number()
    )

  truth_cols <- tibble::tibble(
    turn = integer(),
    borough_index = integer(),
    gss_code = character(),
    borough_name = character(),
    incidence = integer(),
    cumulative = integer(),
    deaths = integer(),
    cumulative_deaths = integer(),
    imports = integer(),
    Rt = numeric()
  )

  observation_cols <- tibble::tibble(
    turn_reported = integer(),
    turn_sampled = integer(),
    turn_available = integer(),
    borough_index = integer(),
    gss_code = character(),
    borough_name = character(),
    test_type = character(),
    n_returned = integer(),
    positives = integer(),
    positivity = numeric()
  )

  action_cols <- tibble::tibble(
    turn = integer(),
    borough_index = integer(),
    gss_code = character(),
    borough_name = character(),
    test_type = character(),
    n_allocated = integer(),
    spend = numeric(),
    cost_per_test = numeric(),
    allocation_spend = numeric(),
    intervention_cost = numeric(),
    total_turn_spend = numeric(),
    cumulative_spend = numeric(),
    budget_remaining = numeric(),
    interventions_active = character()
  )

  attr(truth_cols, "pop_reference") <- pop_tbl

  list(
    truth = truth_cols,
    observations = observation_cols,
    actions = action_cols
  )
}

#' Append a turn of hidden truth to the log
#'
#' @param truth_log Existing truth log tibble.
#' @param turn Integer turn index being recorded.
#' @param incidence Integer vector of incidence counts per borough.
#' @param cumulative Integer vector of cumulative counts per borough.
#' @param imports Integer vector of import counts per borough.
#' @param Rt Numeric reproduction number applied on this turn.
#' @param pop_tbl Population table used to supply borough metadata.
#' @return Updated truth log tibble.
#' @export
append_truth_log <- function(truth_log, turn, incidence, cumulative, deaths, cumulative_deaths, imports, Rt, pop_tbl) {
  incidence <- as.integer(incidence)
  cumulative <- as.integer(cumulative)
  deaths <- as.integer(deaths)
  cumulative_deaths <- as.integer(cumulative_deaths)
  imports <- as.integer(imports)

  n <- length(incidence)
  if (length(cumulative) != n || length(deaths) != n ||
      length(cumulative_deaths) != n || length(imports) != n) {
    stop("incidence, cumulative, deaths, cumulative_deaths, and imports must have the same length")
  }

  pop_tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(pop_tbl)
  if (nrow(pop_tbl) != n) {
    stop("pop_tbl row count must match incidence length")
  }

  addition <- pop_tbl |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      borough_index = dplyr::row_number(),
      turn = as.integer(turn),
      incidence = incidence,
      cumulative = cumulative,
      deaths = deaths,
      cumulative_deaths = cumulative_deaths,
      imports = imports,
      Rt = as.numeric(Rt)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      turn,
      borough_index,
      gss_code,
      borough_name,
      incidence,
      cumulative,
      deaths,
      cumulative_deaths,
      imports,
      Rt
    )

  dplyr::bind_rows(truth_log, addition)
}

#' Append observed results for a turn
#'
#' @param observation_log Existing observation log tibble.
#' @param available_results Tibble of results available on the current turn.
#' @param turn_reported Integer turn index when results became visible to the user.
#' @param pop_tbl Population table for borough metadata.
#' @return Updated observation log tibble.
#' @export
append_observation_log <- function(observation_log, available_results, turn_reported, pop_tbl) {
  if (is.null(available_results) || nrow(available_results) == 0) {
    return(observation_log)
  }

  required_cols <- c(
    "borough_index", "borough_name", "type",
    "n", "positives", "turn_sampled", "turn_available"
  )
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(available_results))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("available_results missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  pop_tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(pop_tbl)
  addition <- available_results |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      pop_tbl |>
        dplyr::mutate(borough_index = dplyr::row_number()) |>
        dplyr::select(borough_index, gss_code),
      by = "borough_index"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      turn_reported = as.integer(turn_reported),
      test_type = type,
      n_returned = as.integer(n),
      positives = as.integer(positives),
      positivity = dplyr::if_else(n_returned > 0, positives / n_returned, 0),
      turn_sampled = as.integer(turn_sampled),
      turn_available = as.integer(turn_available)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      turn_reported,
      turn_sampled,
      turn_available,
      borough_index,
      gss_code,
      borough_name,
      test_type,
      n_returned,
      positives,
      positivity
    )

  dplyr::bind_rows(observation_log, addition)
}

#' Append allocation decisions for a turn
#'
#' @param action_log Existing action log tibble.
#' @param turn Integer turn on which allocations were chosen.
#' @param allocations Tibble with columns borough_index, borough_name, n_ag, n_pcr.
#' @param pop_tbl Population table providing `gss_code`.
#' @param costs Named numeric vector with entries `ag` and `pcr`.
#' @param meta Optional list carrying per-turn metadata, e.g. remaining budget.
#' @return Updated action log tibble.
#' @export
append_action_log <- function(action_log, turn, allocations, pop_tbl, costs, meta = list()) {
  required_cols <- c("borough_index", "borough_name", "n_ag", "n_pcr")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(allocations))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("allocations missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  long_allocs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    allocations |>
      dplyr::select(borough_index, borough_name, n = n_ag) |>
      dplyr::mutate(test_type = "ag"),
    allocations |>
      dplyr::select(borough_index, borough_name, n = n_pcr) |>
      dplyr::mutate(test_type = "pcr")
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(n > 0)

  if (nrow(long_allocs) == 0) {
    return(action_log)
  }

  cost_ag <- costs[["ag"]]
  if (is.null(cost_ag)) cost_ag <- 0
  cost_pcr <- costs[["pcr"]]
  if (is.null(cost_pcr)) cost_pcr <- 0
  costs <- c(ag = cost_ag, pcr = cost_pcr)

  pop_tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(pop_tbl) |>
    dplyr::mutate(borough_index = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::select(borough_index, gss_code)

  addition <- long_allocs |>
    dplyr::left_join(pop_tbl, by = "borough_index") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      turn = as.integer(turn),
      n_allocated = as.integer(n),
      cost_per_test = dplyr::if_else(test_type == "ag", costs[["ag"]], costs[["pcr"]]),
      spend = cost_per_test * n_allocated
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-n)

  meta_defaults <- list(
    allocation_spend = sum(addition$spend),
    intervention_cost = 0,
    total_turn_spend = sum(addition$spend),
    cumulative_spend = NA_real_,
    budget_remaining = NA_real_,
    interventions_active = "None"
  )
  meta_full <- utils::modifyList(meta_defaults, meta, keep.null = TRUE)

  addition <- addition |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      allocation_spend = meta_full$allocation_spend,
      intervention_cost = meta_full$intervention_cost,
      total_turn_spend = meta_full$total_turn_spend,
      cumulative_spend = meta_full$cumulative_spend,
      budget_remaining = meta_full$budget_remaining,
      interventions_active = meta_full$interventions_active
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      turn,
      borough_index,
      gss_code,
      borough_name,
      test_type,
      n_allocated,
      spend,
      cost_per_test,
      allocation_spend,
      intervention_cost,
      total_turn_spend,
      cumulative_spend,
      budget_remaining,
      interventions_active
    )

  dplyr::bind_rows(action_log, addition)
}

#' Estimate currently infectious counts using a rolling window
#'
#' @param truth_log Tibble produced by successive calls to `append_truth_log()`.
#'   Must contain columns `turn`, `borough_index`, `borough_name`, and `incidence`.
#' @param turn Integer turn at which to evaluate active infections.
#' @param window Integer number of turns to include (inclusive of `turn`).
#' @return Tibble with columns `borough_index`, `borough_name`, and `active`.
#' @export
compute_active_infections <- function(truth_log, turn, window = 3L) {
  if (missing(truth_log) || is.null(truth_log) || nrow(truth_log) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      borough_index = integer(),
      borough_name = character(),
      active = integer()
    ))
  }

  if (!("turn" %in% names(truth_log)) || !("incidence" %in% names(truth_log))) {
    stop("truth_log must include columns 'turn' and 'incidence'")
  }

  if (!("borough_index" %in% names(truth_log)) || !("borough_name" %in% names(truth_log))) {
    stop("truth_log must include borough_index and borough_name columns")
  }

  if (length(turn) != 1 || !is.numeric(turn) || is.na(turn)) {
    stop("turn must be a single numeric value")
  }

  window <- as.integer(window)
  if (length(window) != 1 || is.na(window) || window < 1) {
    stop("window must be a positive integer")
  }

  turn_val <- as.integer(turn)
  lower_bound <- turn_val - window + 1L

  in_window <- truth_log[truth_log$turn <= turn_val & truth_log$turn >= lower_bound, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(in_window) == 0) {
    base_set <- truth_log[truth_log$turn <= turn_val, c("borough_index", "borough_name"), drop = FALSE]
    base_set <- unique(base_set)
    if (nrow(base_set) == 0) {
      base_set <- truth_log[, c("borough_index", "borough_name"), drop = FALSE]
      base_set <- unique(base_set)
    }
    if (nrow(base_set) == 0) {
      return(tibble::tibble(
        borough_index = integer(),
        borough_name = character(),
        active = integer()
      ))
    }
    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        borough_index = base_set$borough_index,
        borough_name = base_set$borough_name,
        active = integer(nrow(base_set))
      )
    )
  }

  all_boros <- truth_log[truth_log$turn <= turn_val, c("borough_index", "borough_name"), drop = FALSE]
  all_boros <- unique(all_boros)

  active <- in_window |>
    dplyr::group_by(borough_index, borough_name) |>
    dplyr::summarise(active = sum(incidence, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  result <- dplyr::right_join(
    active,
    tibble::as_tibble(all_boros),
    by = c("borough_index", "borough_name")
  )
  result$active[is.na(result$active)] <- 0L
  result
}
